questions.q: A solid cylinder rotates about its axis from rest with a constant angular acceleration. If the angle it rotates during the $3^{\text{rd}}$ second of its motion is $20$ rad, the angular velocity of the cylinder at the end of the $4^{\text{th}}$ second is :
questions.question: A solid cylinder rotates about its axis from rest with a constant angular acceleration. If the angle it rotates during the $3^{\text{rd}}$ second of its motion is $20$ rad, the angular velocity of the cylinder at the end of the $4^{\text{th}}$ second is :
questions.solution:
Let the constant angular acceleration be $\alpha$.

The angle rotated during the $n^{\text{th}}$ second is given by:
$\theta_n = \omega_0 + \dfrac{\alpha}{2}(2n - 1)$

Given that the cylinder starts from rest ($\omega_0 = 0$) and $\theta_3 = 20$ rad for $n = 3$:
$20 = 0 + \dfrac{\alpha}{2}(2(3) - 1)$
$20 = \dfrac{5\alpha}{2}$
$\alpha = 8 \text{ rad/s}^2$

The angular velocity at the end of the $4^{\text{th}}$ second ($t = 4$ s) is:
$\omega = \omega_0 + \alpha t$
$\omega = 0 + 8 \times 4 = 32 \text{ rad/s}$

Answer: $32$ rad/s

questions.q: A uniform solid sphere of radius $10 \text{ cm}$ has a radius of gyration of $11 \text{ cm}$ about an axis parallel to its diameter. The perpendicular distance of this axis from the centre of the sphere is ________ $\text{cm}$.
questions.question: A uniform solid sphere of radius $10 \text{ cm}$ has a radius of gyration of $11 \text{ cm}$ about an axis parallel to its diameter. The perpendicular distance of this axis from the centre of the sphere is ________ $\text{cm}$.
questions.solution:
Using the parallel axis theorem for the radius of gyration:
$k^2 = k_{cm}^2 + d^2$
For a uniform solid sphere, the square of the radius of gyration about its central diameter is:
$k_{cm}^2 = \dfrac{2}{5}R^2$
Given $R = 10 \text{ cm}$ and $k = 11 \text{ cm}$:
$(11)^2 = \dfrac{2}{5}(10)^2 + d^2$
$121 = 40 + d^2$
$d^2 = 81$
$d = 9 \text{ cm}$

Answer: $9$

questions.q:
A non-uniform rod AB of mass $M$ and length $L$ is suspended horizontally by two vertical inextensible strings attached at its ends A and B. The linear mass density of the rod is proportional to the distance from end A. If the string at end A is suddenly cut, the tension in the string at end B immediately after the cut is
($g$ is acceleration due to gravity)
questions.question:
A non-uniform rod AB of mass $M$ and length $L$ is suspended horizontally by two vertical inextensible strings attached at its ends A and B. The linear mass density of the rod is proportional to the distance from end A. If the string at end A is suddenly cut, the tension in the string at end B immediately after the cut is
($g$ is acceleration due to gravity)
questions.solution:
Let the linear mass density of the rod be $\lambda = cx$, where $x$ is the distance from end A.
The total mass of the rod is:
$M = \int_{0}^{L} cx \, dx = \dfrac{cL^2}{2} \Rightarrow c = \dfrac{2M}{L^2}$
The position of the center of mass from A is:
$x_{cm} = \dfrac{1}{M} \int_{0}^{L} x(cx) \, dx = \dfrac{1}{M} \left( \dfrac{cL^3}{3} \right) = \dfrac{2L}{3}$
So, the distance of the center of mass from end B is $L - \dfrac{2L}{3} = \dfrac{L}{3}$.
When the string at A is cut, the rod rotates about end B.
The moment of inertia of the rod about B is:
$I_B = \int_{0}^{L} (L-x)^2 (cx) \, dx = c \int_{0}^{L} (L^2x - 2Lx^2 + x^3) \, dx$
$I_B = c \left( \dfrac{L^4}{2} - \dfrac{2L^4}{3} + \dfrac{L^4}{4} \right) = c \left( \dfrac{L^4}{12} \right)$
Substituting $c = \dfrac{2M}{L^2}$, we get $I_B = \dfrac{ML^2}{6}$.
Torque about B is provided by the weight acting at the center of mass:
$\tau_B = Mg \left( \dfrac{L}{3} \right)$
Angular acceleration $\alpha$ is:
$\alpha = \dfrac{\tau_B}{I_B} = \dfrac{\dfrac{MgL}{3}}{\dfrac{ML^2}{6}} = \dfrac{2g}{L}$
The downward linear acceleration of the center of mass is:
$a_{cm} = \alpha \left( \dfrac{L}{3} \right) = \dfrac{2g}{3}$
Applying Newton's second law for the vertical motion of the center of mass:
$Mg - T_B = Ma_{cm}$
$T_B = Mg - M\left(\dfrac{2g}{3}\right) = \dfrac{Mg}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{Mg}{3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Three identical particles, each of mass $2\text{ kg}$, are placed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of side $3\text{ m}$. The moment of inertia of the system about an axis perpendicular to the plane of the triangle and passing through its centroid is ________ $\text{kg m}^2$.
questions.question: Three identical particles, each of mass $2\text{ kg}$, are placed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of side $3\text{ m}$. The moment of inertia of the system about an axis perpendicular to the plane of the triangle and passing through its centroid is ________ $\text{kg m}^2$.
questions.solution:
Let the side of the equilateral triangle be $a = 3\text{ m}$ and the mass of each particle be $m = 2\text{ kg}$.

The distance $r$ of any vertex from the centroid of an equilateral triangle is given by:
$r = \dfrac{a}{\sqrt{3}}$

The moment of inertia of the system about an axis passing through the centroid and perpendicular to the plane is the sum of the moments of inertia of the three particles.

$I = m_1 r_1^2 + m_2 r_2^2 + m_3 r_3^2$

Since all particles have the same mass and are at the same distance from the centroid:
$I = 3 \times m \left(\dfrac{a}{\sqrt{3}}\right)^2$
$I = 3 \times m \times \dfrac{a^2}{3} = m a^2$

Substitute the given values:
$I = 2 \times (3)^2 = 2 \times 9 = 18\text{ kg m}^2$.

Answer: $18$

questions.q: A particle of mass $m$ moves in the $xy$-plane such that its position vector at time $t$ is given by $\vec{r} = R(\cos \omega t \hat{i} + \sin \omega t \hat{j})$, where $R$ and $\omega$ are positive constants. If $\vec{v}$ and $\vec{a}$ represent the velocity and acceleration vectors of the particle respectively, and $\vec{L}$ represents its angular momentum about the origin, then the direction of the vector $(\vec{v} \times \vec{a})$ is
questions.question: A particle of mass $m$ moves in the $xy$-plane such that its position vector at time $t$ is given by $\vec{r} = R(\cos \omega t \hat{i} + \sin \omega t \hat{j})$, where $R$ and $\omega$ are positive constants. If $\vec{v}$ and $\vec{a}$ represent the velocity and acceleration vectors of the particle respectively, and $\vec{L}$ represents its angular momentum about the origin, then the direction of the vector $(\vec{v} \times \vec{a})$ is
options: The zero vector, having no defined direction
questions.solution:
The position vector is given by $\vec{r} = R(\cos \omega t \hat{i} + \sin \omega t \hat{j})$.

Differentiating with respect to time to find velocity:
$\vec{v} = \dfrac{d\vec{r}}{dt} = \omega R(-\sin \omega t \hat{i} + \cos \omega t \hat{j})$

Differentiating velocity to find acceleration:
$\vec{a} = \dfrac{d\vec{v}}{dt} = -\omega^2 R(\cos \omega t \hat{i} + \sin \omega t \hat{j}) = -\omega^2 \vec{r}$

Now, compute the cross product $(\vec{v} \times \vec{a})$:
$\vec{v} \times \vec{a} = [\omega R(-\sin \omega t \hat{i} + \cos \omega t \hat{j})] \times [-\omega^2 R(\cos \omega t \hat{i} + \sin \omega t \hat{j})]$
$\vec{v} \times \vec{a} = -\omega^3 R^2 [(-\sin \omega t)(\sin \omega t)(\hat{i} \times \hat{j}) + (\cos \omega t)(\cos \omega t)(\hat{j} \times \hat{i})]$
$\vec{v} \times \vec{a} = -\omega^3 R^2 [-\sin^2 \omega t \hat{k} - \cos^2 \omega t \hat{k}] = \omega^3 R^2 \hat{k}$

The angular momentum $\vec{L}$ about the origin is:
$\vec{L} = \vec{r} \times m\vec{v} = m [R(\cos \omega t \hat{i} + \sin \omega t \hat{j})] \times [\omega R(-\sin \omega t \hat{i} + \cos \omega t \hat{j})]$
$\vec{L} = m \omega R^2 (\cos^2 \omega t \hat{k} + \sin^2 \omega t \hat{k}) = m \omega R^2 \hat{k}$

Both $(\vec{v} \times \vec{a})$ and $\vec{L}$ are directed along the positive $z$-axis ($\hat{k}$). Therefore, $(\vec{v} \times \vec{a})$ is parallel to the direction of $\vec{L}$.

Answer: Parallel to the direction of $\vec{L}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle of mass $m$ is projected in the $x$-$y$ plane such that its trajectory is given by the equation $y = \alpha x - \beta x^2$, where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are positive constants and $y$ is the vertical upward direction. The magnitude of the angular momentum of the particle about the origin when it is at its maximum height is (where $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity)
questions.question: A particle of mass $m$ is projected in the $x$-$y$ plane such that its trajectory is given by the equation $y = \alpha x - \beta x^2$, where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are positive constants and $y$ is the vertical upward direction. The magnitude of the angular momentum of the particle about the origin when it is at its maximum height is (where $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity)
questions.solution:
The equation of trajectory is given by $y = \alpha x - \beta x^2$.

Comparing this with the standard equation of projectile motion $y = x \tan\theta - \dfrac{g x^2}{2 u^2 \cos^2\theta}$, we get:
$\tan\theta = \alpha$
$\dfrac{g}{2 u^2 \cos^2\theta} = \beta \implies u \cos\theta = \sqrt{\dfrac{g}{2\beta}}$

The horizontal component of velocity is constant throughout the motion and equals $v_x = u \cos\theta = \sqrt{\dfrac{g}{2\beta}}$.

At the maximum height, the vertical component of velocity is zero, so the velocity vector is purely horizontal: $\vec{v} = v_x \hat{i}$.

The maximum height $H$ can be found by maximizing $y$. For $y = \alpha x - \beta x^2$, the maximum occurs at $x = \dfrac{\alpha}{2\beta}$.
Substituting this value, $H = \alpha \left(\dfrac{\alpha}{2\beta}\right) - \beta \left(\dfrac{\alpha}{2\beta}\right)^2 = \dfrac{\alpha^2}{4\beta}$.

The position vector of the particle at the highest point is $\vec{r} = \dfrac{\alpha}{2\beta} \hat{i} + H \hat{j}$.

The angular momentum about the origin is $\vec{L} = \vec{r} \times (m\vec{v}) = \left( \dfrac{\alpha}{2\beta} \hat{i} + H \hat{j} \right) \times \left( m v_x \hat{i} \right) = - m H v_x \hat{k}$.

The magnitude of the angular momentum is:
$|\vec{L}| = m H v_x = m \left( \dfrac{\alpha^2}{4\beta} \right) \sqrt{\dfrac{g}{2\beta}}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{m \alpha^2}{4\beta} \sqrt{\dfrac{g}{2\beta}}$

questions.q: A uniform rod of length $100\text{ cm}$ and mass $3\text{ kg}$ is suspended horizontally by two vertical strings attached at its ends (at the $0\text{ cm}$ and $100\text{ cm}$ marks). A block of mass $6\text{ kg}$ is placed on the rod at a distance $x\text{ cm}$ from the $0\text{ cm}$ end. If the tension in the string at the $0\text{ cm}$ mark is twice the tension in the string at the $100\text{ cm}$ mark, the value of $x$ is ________.
questions.question: A uniform rod of length $100\text{ cm}$ and mass $3\text{ kg}$ is suspended horizontally by two vertical strings attached at its ends (at the $0\text{ cm}$ and $100\text{ cm}$ marks). A block of mass $6\text{ kg}$ is placed on the rod at a distance $x\text{ cm}$ from the $0\text{ cm}$ end. If the tension in the string at the $0\text{ cm}$ mark is twice the tension in the string at the $100\text{ cm}$ mark, the value of $x$ is ________.
questions.solution:
Let $T_1$ and $T_2$ be the tensions in the strings at the $0\text{ cm}$ and $100\text{ cm}$ marks, respectively.

Given that $T_1 = 2T_2$.

For translational equilibrium, the total upward force equals the total downward force:

$T_1 + T_2 = 3g + 6g = 9g$

$2T_2 + T_2 = 9g \Rightarrow 3T_2 = 9g \Rightarrow T_2 = 3g$

For rotational equilibrium, the net torque about the $0\text{ cm}$ end must be zero. The forces producing torque are the weight of the rod (acting at $50\text{ cm}$), the weight of the block (acting at $x\text{ cm}$), and the tension $T_2$ (acting at $100\text{ cm}$).

$(3g \times 50) + (6g \times x) = T_2 \times 100$

$150g + 6gx = 3g \times 100$

$150 + 6x = 300$

$6x = 150$

$x = 25$

Answer: $25$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Four particles of masses $1\text{ kg}$, $2\text{ kg}$, $3\text{ kg}$, and $4\text{ kg}$ are placed at the corners $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$ respectively of a square of side $10\text{ m}$. The moment of inertia of the system about an axis perpendicular to the plane of the square and passing through the center of mass of the system is ________ $\text{kg m}^2$.
questions.question: Four particles of masses $1\text{ kg}$, $2\text{ kg}$, $3\text{ kg}$, and $4\text{ kg}$ are placed at the corners $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$ respectively of a square of side $10\text{ m}$. The moment of inertia of the system about an axis perpendicular to the plane of the square and passing through the center of mass of the system is ________ $\text{kg m}^2$.
questions.solution:
Let the corner $A$ be at the origin $(0,0)$. The coordinates of the corners are:
$A(0, 0)$ with $m_A = 1\text{ kg}$
$B(10, 0)$ with $m_B = 2\text{ kg}$
$C(10, 10)$ with $m_C = 3\text{ kg}$
$D(0, 10)$ with $m_D = 4\text{ kg}$

Total mass of the system, $M = 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10\text{ kg}$.

The coordinates of the center of mass $(X_{cm}, Y_{cm})$ are:
$X_{cm} = \dfrac{m_A x_A + m_B x_B + m_C x_C + m_D x_D}{M}$
$X_{cm} = \dfrac{1(0) + 2(10) + 3(10) + 4(0)}{10} = \dfrac{50}{10} = 5\text{ m}$

$Y_{cm} = \dfrac{m_A y_A + m_B y_B + m_C y_C + m_D y_D}{M}$
$Y_{cm} = \dfrac{1(0) + 2(0) + 3(10) + 4(10)}{10} = \dfrac{70}{10} = 7\text{ m}$

The center of mass is at $(5, 7)$.

Now, we find the square of the distance of each particle from the center of mass:
$r_A^2 = (0 - 5)^2 + (0 - 7)^2 = 25 + 49 = 74\text{ m}^2$
$r_B^2 = (10 - 5)^2 + (0 - 7)^2 = 25 + 49 = 74\text{ m}^2$
$r_C^2 = (10 - 5)^2 + (10 - 7)^2 = 25 + 9 = 34\text{ m}^2$
$r_D^2 = (0 - 5)^2 + (10 - 7)^2 = 25 + 9 = 34\text{ m}^2$

The moment of inertia about the center of mass is:
$I_{cm} = m_A r_A^2 + m_B r_B^2 + m_C r_C^2 + m_D r_D^2$
$I_{cm} = 1(74) + 2(74) + 3(34) + 4(34)$
$I_{cm} = 74 + 148 + 102 + 136$
$I_{cm} = 460\text{ kg m}^2$.

Alternatively, using the parallel axis theorem:
$I_A = 1(0) + 2(10^2) + 3(10^2 + 10^2) + 4(10^2) = 0 + 200 + 600 + 400 = 1200\text{ kg m}^2$.
Distance squared from $A$ to CoM is $d^2 = 5^2 + 7^2 = 74\text{ m}^2$.
$I_{cm} = I_A - M d^2 = 1200 - 10(74) = 1200 - 740 = 460\text{ kg m}^2$.

Answer: $460$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle executes simple harmonic motion of time period $T$. At $t = 0$, it starts from the extreme position. If the maximum kinetic energy of the particle is $K_0$, the work done by the restoring force during the time interval $t = 0$ to $t = \dfrac{T}{6}$ is
questions.question: A particle executes simple harmonic motion of time period $T$. At $t = 0$, it starts from the extreme position. If the maximum kinetic energy of the particle is $K_0$, the work done by the restoring force during the time interval $t = 0$ to $t = \dfrac{T}{6}$ is
questions.solution:
The equation of motion for a particle starting from the extreme position is $x(t) = A \cos\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{T}t\right)$.

At $t = 0$, the position is $x = A$. The initial potential energy is $U_i = \dfrac{1}{2}m\omega^2 A^2 = K_0$ (since maximum kinetic energy equals total energy).

At $t = \dfrac{T}{6}$, the position is:
$x = A \cos\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{T} \times \dfrac{T}{6}\right) = A \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{A}{2}$

The final potential energy at this instant is:
$U_f = \dfrac{1}{2}m\omega^2 \left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{4} \left(\dfrac{1}{2}m\omega^2 A^2\right) = \dfrac{K_0}{4}$

The work done by the conservative restoring force is equal to the negative of the change in potential energy:
$W = -\Delta U = U_i - U_f$

$W = K_0 - \dfrac{K_0}{4} = \dfrac{3K_0}{4}$

Answer: $\dfrac{3K_0}{4}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solid sphere and a hollow sphere of the same mass have the same radius of gyration about their respective diametric axes. If the ratio of the radius of the solid sphere to the radius of the hollow sphere is $\sqrt{\dfrac{x}{3}}$, then the value of $x$ is _______.
questions.question: A solid sphere and a hollow sphere of the same mass have the same radius of gyration about their respective diametric axes. If the ratio of the radius of the solid sphere to the radius of the hollow sphere is $\sqrt{\dfrac{x}{3}}$, then the value of $x$ is _______.
questions.solution:
Let the mass of both spheres be $m$.

The moment of inertia of the solid sphere about its diameter is $I_1 = \dfrac{2}{5}mR_1^2$, so its radius of gyration is $k_1 = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{5}}R_1$.

The moment of inertia of the hollow sphere about its diameter is $I_2 = \dfrac{2}{3}mR_2^2$, so its radius of gyration is $k_2 = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}R_2$.

Given that $k_1 = k_2$, we have:
$\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{5}}R_1 = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}R_2$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{R_1}{R_2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{3}}$

Comparing this with the given ratio $\sqrt{\dfrac{x}{3}}$, we get $x = 5$.

Answer: $5$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform square plate of mass $500\text{ g}$ and side length $20\text{ cm}$ rotates about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its plane with an angular speed of $4\text{ rad s}^{-1}$. The moment of inertia of the plate about an axis coinciding with one of its edges is numerically equal to $\dfrac{x}{10}$ times its angular momentum about the axis of rotation. The value of $x$ is
questions.question: A uniform square plate of mass $500\text{ g}$ and side length $20\text{ cm}$ rotates about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its plane with an angular speed of $4\text{ rad s}^{-1}$. The moment of inertia of the plate about an axis coinciding with one of its edges is numerically equal to $\dfrac{x}{10}$ times its angular momentum about the axis of rotation. The value of $x$ is
questions.solution:
The moment of inertia of a uniform square plate about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its plane is
$I_{\perp} = \dfrac{M(a^2 + a^2)}{12} = \dfrac{Ma^2}{6}$

The angular momentum about this axis of rotation is
$L = I_{\perp}\omega = \left(\dfrac{Ma^2}{6}\right) \times 4 = \dfrac{2}{3}Ma^2$

The moment of inertia about an axis passing through its centre and parallel to an edge is
$I_{\text{cm}} = \dfrac{Ma^2}{12}$

Using the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia about one of its edges (which is at a distance of $a/2$ from the parallel centroidal axis) is
$I_{\text{edge}} = I_{\text{cm}} + M\left(\dfrac{a}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{Ma^2}{12} + \dfrac{Ma^2}{4} = \dfrac{Ma^2}{3}$

According to the given condition,
$I_{\text{edge}} = \dfrac{x}{10} \times L$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{Ma^2}{3} = \dfrac{x}{10} \times \dfrac{2}{3}Ma^2$
$\Rightarrow 1 = \dfrac{2x}{10}$
$\Rightarrow x = 5$

Answer: $5$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform rigid rod of weight $W$ is hinged to the ground at its lower end. It is held in equilibrium at an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal by a horizontal string attached to its upper end. The tension in the horizontal string is :
questions.question: A uniform rigid rod of weight $W$ is hinged to the ground at its lower end. It is held in equilibrium at an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal by a horizontal string attached to its upper end. The tension in the horizontal string is :
questions.solution:
Let the length of the rod be $L$.

The rod is in rotational equilibrium. Taking torque about the hinge at the ground, the forces producing torque are the weight of the rod $W$ and the tension in the string $T$.

The weight $W$ acts vertically downwards at the center of mass of the rod, which is at a distance of $\dfrac{L}{2}$ from the hinge. The perpendicular distance of the line of action of $W$ from the hinge is $\dfrac{L}{2} \cos \theta$.

The tension $T$ acts horizontally at the upper end of the rod, which is at a distance $L$ from the hinge. The perpendicular distance of the line of action of $T$ from the hinge is $L \sin \theta$.

Equating the torques to maintain equilibrium:
$W \left( \dfrac{L}{2} \cos \theta \right) = T (L \sin \theta)$

Solving for $T$:
$T = \dfrac{W \cos \theta}{2 \sin \theta} = \dfrac{W}{2} \cot \theta$

Answer: $\dfrac{W}{2} \cot \theta$

questions.q: A uniform solid sphere of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is melted and recast into a uniform solid cylinder of the same radius $R$. Let $k_1$ be the radius of gyration of the initial solid sphere about its diameter, and $k_2$ be the radius of gyration of the recast solid cylinder about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its length. If the ratio $\dfrac{k_1}{k_2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{x}{215}}$, then the value of $x$ is :
questions.question: A uniform solid sphere of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is melted and recast into a uniform solid cylinder of the same radius $R$. Let $k_1$ be the radius of gyration of the initial solid sphere about its diameter, and $k_2$ be the radius of gyration of the recast solid cylinder about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its length. If the ratio $\dfrac{k_1}{k_2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{x}{215}}$, then the value of $x$ is :
questions.solution:
Since the solid sphere is melted and recast into a solid cylinder, the volume remains conserved.
Volume of sphere = Volume of cylinder
$\dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = \pi R^2 L$
This gives the length of the cylinder as $L = \dfrac{4}{3}R$.

For the initial solid sphere, the moment of inertia about its diameter is:
$I_1 = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2$
Thus, $k_1^2 = \dfrac{2}{5}R^2$.

For the recast solid cylinder, the moment of inertia about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its length is:
$I_2 = M\left(\dfrac{R^2}{4} + \dfrac{L^2}{12}\right)$
Substituting $L = \dfrac{4}{3}R$ into the equation:
$I_2 = M\left(\dfrac{R^2}{4} + \dfrac{(16/9)R^2}{12}\right) = M\left(\dfrac{R^2}{4} + \dfrac{4R^2}{27}\right)$
$I_2 = M\left(\dfrac{27R^2 + 16R^2}{108}\right) = \dfrac{43}{108}MR^2$
Thus, $k_2^2 = \dfrac{43}{108}R^2$.

The ratio of their radii of gyration is:
$\dfrac{k_1}{k_2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{k_1^2}{k_2^2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2/5}{43/108}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{216}{215}}$

Comparing this with $\sqrt{\dfrac{x}{215}}$, we get $x = 216$.

Answer: $216$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solid sphere and a hollow sphere have the same mass and the same radius. Their radii of gyration are measured about axes that are tangential to their respective surfaces. If the ratio of the radius of gyration of the solid sphere to that of the hollow sphere is $\dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{5}$, then the value of $x$ is _______.
questions.question: A solid sphere and a hollow sphere have the same mass and the same radius. Their radii of gyration are measured about axes that are tangential to their respective surfaces. If the ratio of the radius of gyration of the solid sphere to that of the hollow sphere is $\dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{5}$, then the value of $x$ is _______.
questions.solution:
Let the mass of both spheres be $m$ and their radius be $R$.

Using the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia of the solid sphere about a tangential axis is:
$I_{solid} = I_{cm} + mR^2 = \dfrac{2}{5}mR^2 + mR^2 = \dfrac{7}{5}mR^2$
Its radius of gyration is $k_{solid} = \sqrt{\dfrac{7}{5}}R$.

Similarly, the moment of inertia of the hollow sphere about a tangential axis is:
$I_{hollow} = I_{cm} + mR^2 = \dfrac{2}{3}mR^2 + mR^2 = \dfrac{5}{3}mR^2$
Its radius of gyration is $k_{hollow} = \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{3}}R$.

The ratio of their radii of gyration is:
$\dfrac{k_{solid}}{k_{hollow}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{7/5}R}{\sqrt{5/3}R} = \sqrt{\dfrac{7}{5} \times \dfrac{3}{5}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{21}{25}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{21}}{5}$

Comparing this with $\dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{5}$, we get $x = 21$.

Answer: $21$

It is held stationary in a vertical plane such that its lower edge is perfectly horizontal. To maintain this equilibrium, a force $F$ is applied at the top-right corner B. The force $F$ is directed exactly perpendicular to the diagonal OB. Taking $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$, the magnitude of the force $F$ is :
questions.question: A uniform square plate of mass $2\sqrt{2} \text{ kg}$ and side length $L$ is pivoted smoothly at its bottom-left corner O. It is held stationary in a vertical plane such that its lower edge is perfectly horizontal. To maintain this equilibrium, a force $F$ is applied at the top-right corner B. The force $F$ is directed exactly perpendicular to the diagonal OB. Taking $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$, the magnitude of the force $F$ is :
questions.solution:
For the square plate to remain stationary, the net torque about the pivot O must be zero.

The weight of the uniform square plate acts downwards through its center of mass. The horizontal distance from the pivot O to the line of action of the weight is half the side length, i.e., $\dfrac{L}{2}$.
The clockwise torque due to gravity is:
$\tau_{g} = mg \times \dfrac{L}{2} = (2\sqrt{2})(10)\left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right) = 10\sqrt{2}L$

The applied force $F$ acts at corner B, and its line of action is perpendicular to the diagonal OB. The perpendicular distance from the pivot O to the line of action of $F$ is simply the length of the diagonal OB.
Length of diagonal OB $= L\sqrt{2}$
The counter-clockwise torque due to $F$ is:
$\tau_{F} = F \times L\sqrt{2}$

Equating the clockwise and counter-clockwise torques:
$F \times L\sqrt{2} = 10\sqrt{2}L$
$F = 10 \text{ N}$

Answer: $10 \text{ N}$

questions.q: Two identical uniform solid spheres, each of mass $5 \text{ kg}$ and radius $10 \text{ cm}$, are connected by a uniform thin rod of mass $3 \text{ kg}$ and length $20 \text{ cm}$. The ends of the rod are attached to the surfaces of the spheres such that the centers of the spheres and the rod lie on a single straight line. The system is rotated about an axis passing through the center of the rod and perpendicular to it. If the angular acceleration of the system is $20 \text{ rad/s}^2$, the applied torque is:
questions.question: Two identical uniform solid spheres, each of mass $5 \text{ kg}$ and radius $10 \text{ cm}$, are connected by a uniform thin rod of mass $3 \text{ kg}$ and length $20 \text{ cm}$. The ends of the rod are attached to the surfaces of the spheres such that the centers of the spheres and the rod lie on a single straight line. The system is rotated about an axis passing through the center of the rod and perpendicular to it. If the angular acceleration of the system is $20 \text{ rad/s}^2$, the applied torque is:
questions.solution:
Let the axis of rotation be passing through the center of the rod.

Distance of the center of each sphere from the axis of rotation, $d = \dfrac{L}{2} + R = \dfrac{20}{2} + 10 = 20 \text{ cm} = 0.2 \text{ m}$.

Moment of inertia of the rod about the axis, $I_{\text{rod}} = \dfrac{1}{12}M_{\text{r}}L^2 = \dfrac{1}{12} \times 3 \times (0.2)^2 = 0.01 \text{ kg m}^2$.

Moment of inertia of one solid sphere about the axis of rotation (using parallel axis theorem),
$I_{\text{sphere}} = \dfrac{2}{5}M_{\text{s}}R^2 + M_{\text{s}}d^2 = \dfrac{2}{5} \times 5 \times (0.1)^2 + 5 \times (0.2)^2 = 0.02 + 0.20 = 0.22 \text{ kg m}^2$.

Total moment of inertia of the system, $I = I_{\text{rod}} + 2I_{\text{sphere}} = 0.01 + 2(0.22) = 0.45 \text{ kg m}^2$.

The applied torque is given by $\tau = I\alpha = 0.45 \times 20 = 9 \text{ N m}$.

Answer: $9 \text{ N m}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solid sphere of mass $m$ and radius $R$ is rolling without slipping on a horizontal surface with a translational speed $v$. It then encounters an upward inclined plane. In the first case, the incline is rough enough to support pure rolling, and the sphere reaches a maximum vertical height $h_1$. In the second case, the incline is perfectly smooth, and the sphere reaches a maximum vertical height $h_2$. If the ratio $\dfrac{h_1}{h_2}$ is $\dfrac{x}{5}$, the value of $x$ is ______.
questions.question: A solid sphere of mass $m$ and radius $R$ is rolling without slipping on a horizontal surface with a translational speed $v$. It then encounters an upward inclined plane. In the first case, the incline is rough enough to support pure rolling, and the sphere reaches a maximum vertical height $h_1$. In the second case, the incline is perfectly smooth, and the sphere reaches a maximum vertical height $h_2$. If the ratio $\dfrac{h_1}{h_2}$ is $\dfrac{x}{5}$, the value of $x$ is ______.
questions.solution:
For a solid sphere, the moment of inertia is $I = \dfrac{2}{5}mR^2$, which means $\dfrac{k^2}{R^2} = \dfrac{2}{5}$.

In the first case (rough incline), the sphere rolls without slipping until its translational and rotational velocities both become zero. The total kinetic energy is converted into potential energy:

$mgh_1 = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 \left(1 + \dfrac{k^2}{R^2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 \left(1 + \dfrac{2}{5}\right) = \dfrac{7}{10}mv^2$

$\Rightarrow h_1 = \dfrac{7v^2}{10g}$

In the second case (perfectly smooth incline), there is no friction on the incline to provide a torque. Thus, the angular velocity of the sphere remains constant as it moves up the incline. Only the translational kinetic energy is converted into potential energy:

$mgh_2 = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2$

$\Rightarrow h_2 = \dfrac{v^2}{2g} = \dfrac{5v^2}{10g}$

The ratio of the maximum heights is:

$\dfrac{h_1}{h_2} = \dfrac{\dfrac{7v^2}{10g}}{\dfrac{5v^2}{10g}} = \dfrac{7}{5}$

Given $\dfrac{h_1}{h_2} = \dfrac{x}{5}$, we get $x = 7$.

Answer: $7$

questions.q: A uniform solid sphere of mass $M$ and radius $R$, and a uniform square plate of mass $M$ and side length $2R$ are considered. Let $k_A$ be the radius of gyration of the solid sphere about an axis tangent to its surface, and $k_B$ be the radius of gyration of the square plate about an axis passing through one of its corners and perpendicular to its plane. If the ratio $\dfrac{k_A}{k_B} = \sqrt{\dfrac{21}{x}}$, then the value of $x$ is :
questions.question: A uniform solid sphere of mass $M$ and radius $R$, and a uniform square plate of mass $M$ and side length $2R$ are considered. Let $k_A$ be the radius of gyration of the solid sphere about an axis tangent to its surface, and $k_B$ be the radius of gyration of the square plate about an axis passing through one of its corners and perpendicular to its plane. If the ratio $\dfrac{k_A}{k_B} = \sqrt{\dfrac{21}{x}}$, then the value of $x$ is :
questions.solution:
For the uniform solid sphere, the moment of inertia about its diameter is $I_{cm} = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2$.
Using the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia about a tangent axis is:
$I_A = I_{cm} + MR^2 = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2 + MR^2 = \dfrac{7}{5}MR^2$
Therefore, $k_A^2 = \dfrac{7}{5}R^2$.

For the uniform square plate of side length $a = 2R$, the moment of inertia about an axis passing through its centre of mass and perpendicular to its plane is:
$I_{cm} = \dfrac{M(a^2 + a^2)}{12} = \dfrac{M((2R)^2 + (2R)^2)}{12} = \dfrac{M(8R^2)}{12} = \dfrac{2}{3}MR^2$
The distance $d$ from the centre of the square to one of its corners is half the diagonal:
$d = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}a}{2} = \dfrac{a}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{2R}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}R$
Using the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia about the axis through a corner and perpendicular to the plane is:
$I_B = I_{cm} + Md^2 = \dfrac{2}{3}MR^2 + M(\sqrt{2}R)^2 = \dfrac{2}{3}MR^2 + 2MR^2 = \dfrac{8}{3}MR^2$
Therefore, $k_B^2 = \dfrac{8}{3}R^2$.

The ratio of their radii of gyration is:
$\dfrac{k_A}{k_B} = \sqrt{\dfrac{k_A^2}{k_B^2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{7/5}{8/3}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{21}{40}}$

Comparing this with $\sqrt{\dfrac{21}{x}}$, we get $x = 40$.

Answer: $40$

questions.q:
A uniform solid disc of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is held horizontally and suspended by two identical vertical inextensible strings attached to opposite ends of one of its diameters. If one of the strings is suddenly cut, the tension in the remaining string immediately after the cut is
($g$ is acceleration due to gravity)
questions.question:
A uniform solid disc of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is held horizontally and suspended by two identical vertical inextensible strings attached to opposite ends of one of its diameters. If one of the strings is suddenly cut, the tension in the remaining string immediately after the cut is
($g$ is acceleration due to gravity)
questions.solution:
Let the strings be attached at points A and B, which are the ends of a diameter.
When the string at B is cut, the disc will instantaneously rotate about a horizontal axis passing through A and perpendicular to the diameter AB (i.e., the tangent to the disc at A).
Moment of inertia of the disc about its diameter is $I_{d} = \dfrac{MR^2}{4}$.
By parallel axis theorem, moment of inertia about the tangent at A is:
$I_A = I_{d} + MR^2 = \dfrac{MR^2}{4} + MR^2 = \dfrac{5MR^2}{4}$
Torque about A is provided by the weight of the disc acting at its center of mass (distance $R$ from A):
$\tau_A = MgR$
Angular acceleration $\alpha$ is given by:
$\alpha = \dfrac{\tau_A}{I_A} = \dfrac{MgR}{\dfrac{5MR^2}{4}} = \dfrac{4g}{5R}$
The downward linear acceleration of the center of mass is:
$a_{cm} = \alpha R = \dfrac{4g}{5}$
Applying Newton's second law for the vertical motion of the center of mass:
$Mg - T = Ma_{cm}$
$T = Mg - M\left(\dfrac{4g}{5}\right) = \dfrac{Mg}{5}$

Answer: $\dfrac{Mg}{5}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two identical solid spheres, each of mass $5 \text{ kg}$ and radius $1 \text{ m}$, are fixed with their centers at the ends of a uniform rod of mass $3 \text{ kg}$ and length $4 \text{ m}$. The entire system rotates freely about an axis passing through the midpoint of the rod and perpendicular to its length with an angular speed of $2 \text{ rad/s}$. The rotational kinetic energy of the system is $\ldots\ldots \text{ J}$.
questions.question: Two identical solid spheres, each of mass $5 \text{ kg}$ and radius $1 \text{ m}$, are fixed with their centers at the ends of a uniform rod of mass $3 \text{ kg}$ and length $4 \text{ m}$. The entire system rotates freely about an axis passing through the midpoint of the rod and perpendicular to its length with an angular speed of $2 \text{ rad/s}$. The rotational kinetic energy of the system is $\ldots\ldots \text{ J}$.
questions.solution:
The total moment of inertia of the system is the sum of the moment of inertia of the rod and the moments of inertia of the two spheres.

The moment of inertia of the uniform rod about its perpendicular bisector is:

$I_{\text{rod}} = \dfrac{1}{12}M_{\text{rod}}L^2 = \dfrac{1}{12}(3)(4)^2 = 4 \text{ kg m}^2$

The distance from the axis of rotation to the center of each sphere is half the length of the rod:

$d = \dfrac{L}{2} = \dfrac{4}{2} = 2 \text{ m}$

Using the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia of one solid sphere about the axis of rotation is:

$I_{\text{sphere}} = \dfrac{2}{5}mR^2 + md^2$

$I_{\text{sphere}} = \dfrac{2}{5}(5)(1)^2 + 5(2)^2 = 2 + 20 = 22 \text{ kg m}^2$

The total moment of inertia of the system is:

$I_{\text{total}} = I_{\text{rod}} + 2I_{\text{sphere}} = 4 + 2(22) = 48 \text{ kg m}^2$

The rotational kinetic energy of the system is given by:

$K = \dfrac{1}{2}I_{\text{total}}\omega^2$

$K = \dfrac{1}{2}(48)(2)^2 = 24 \times 4 = 96 \text{ J}$

Answer: $96$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solid sphere of radius $R$ and a thin hollow cylinder of radius $R$ have the same radius of gyration about their respective axes of rotation. The hollow cylinder rotates about its central geometric axis. The solid sphere rotates about an axis parallel to its diameter, located at a perpendicular distance $d$ from its centre. If $d = \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{x}} R$, the value of $x$ is _____.
questions.question: A solid sphere of radius $R$ and a thin hollow cylinder of radius $R$ have the same radius of gyration about their respective axes of rotation. The hollow cylinder rotates about its central geometric axis. The solid sphere rotates about an axis parallel to its diameter, located at a perpendicular distance $d$ from its centre. If $d = \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{x}} R$, the value of $x$ is _____.
questions.solution:
The moment of inertia of a thin hollow cylinder about its central geometric axis is $I_{\text{cyl}} = mR^2$.

Its radius of gyration squared is $k_{\text{cyl}}^2 = R^2$.

For the solid sphere, using the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia about the given axis is $I_{\text{sph}} = \dfrac{2}{5}mR^2 + md^2$.

Its radius of gyration squared is $k_{\text{sph}}^2 = \dfrac{2}{5}R^2 + d^2$.

Given that the radii of gyration are equal:

$R^2 = \dfrac{2}{5}R^2 + d^2$

$\Rightarrow d^2 = R^2 - \dfrac{2}{5}R^2 = \dfrac{3}{5}R^2$

$\Rightarrow d = \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{5}} R$

Comparing this with $d = \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{x}} R$, we get $x = 5$.

Answer: $5$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A steering wheel is constructed from a thin uniform outer ring of mass $M$ and radius $L$, and four mutually perpendicular spokes. The spokes are identical uniform solid cylinders, each of radius $R$ and length $L$, connecting the center of the wheel to the outer ring. The total mass of the four spokes combined is also $M$. The total moment of inertia of the wheel about its central axis (perpendicular to the plane of the wheel) is :
questions.question: A steering wheel is constructed from a thin uniform outer ring of mass $M$ and radius $L$, and four mutually perpendicular spokes. The spokes are identical uniform solid cylinders, each of radius $R$ and length $L$, connecting the center of the wheel to the outer ring. The total mass of the four spokes combined is also $M$. The total moment of inertia of the wheel about its central axis (perpendicular to the plane of the wheel) is :
questions.solution:
The total moment of inertia of the wheel is the sum of the moment of inertia of the outer ring and the four spokes.

For the thin uniform outer ring of mass $M$ and radius $L$, the moment of inertia about the central axis is:
$I_{\text{ring}} = M L^{2}$

The four spokes have a total mass of $M$, so each spoke has a mass $m = \dfrac{M}{4}$.
The central axis is perpendicular to the length of each spoke and passes through one of its ends. Using the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia of one spoke about this axis is:
$I_{\text{spoke}} = I_{\text{cm}} + m\left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right)^{2}$
$I_{\text{spoke}} = \left(\dfrac{m R^{2}}{4} + \dfrac{mL^{2}}{12}\right) + \dfrac{mL^{2}}{4} = \dfrac{m R^{2}}{4} + \dfrac{mL^{2}}{3}$

Since there are four identical spokes, their combined moment of inertia is:
$I_{\text{spokes, total}} = 4 \times \left(\dfrac{m R^{2}}{4} + \dfrac{mL^{2}}{3}\right) = 4 \times \left(\dfrac{M}{16} R^{2} + \dfrac{M}{12} L^{2}\right) = \dfrac{M R^{2}}{4} + \dfrac{M L^{2}}{3}$

The total moment of inertia of the wheel is:
$I_{\text{total}} = I_{\text{ring}} + I_{\text{spokes, total}} = M L^{2} + \dfrac{M R^{2}}{4} + \dfrac{M L^{2}}{3} = \dfrac{1}{4} M R^{2} + \dfrac{4}{3} M L^{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{4} M R^{2} + \dfrac{4}{3} M L^{2}$

questions.q: A solid cylinder of mass $m$ and radius $R$ is suspended by a light inextensible string wrapped around it. The other end of the string is fixed to a point $O$ on the ceiling. The cylinder is released from rest and falls vertically, unwinding the string without slipping. At an instant when the downward speed of the center of mass of the cylinder is $v$, the magnitude of the angular momentum of the cylinder about the point $O$ is expressed as $\dfrac{x}{2} m v R$. The value of $x$ is
questions.question: A solid cylinder of mass $m$ and radius $R$ is suspended by a light inextensible string wrapped around it. The other end of the string is fixed to a point $O$ on the ceiling. The cylinder is released from rest and falls vertically, unwinding the string without slipping. At an instant when the downward speed of the center of mass of the cylinder is $v$, the magnitude of the angular momentum of the cylinder about the point $O$ is expressed as $\dfrac{x}{2} m v R$. The value of $x$ is
questions.solution:
The cylinder undergoes both translational and rotational motion.

The velocity of the center of mass is $v$ downwards. Since the string is fixed at $O$ and unwinds without slipping, the angular velocity of the cylinder is $\omega = \dfrac{v}{R}$.

The angular momentum of the cylinder about the point $O$ is the sum of its translational and rotational angular momenta:
$L_O = L_{\text{trans}} + L_{\text{rot}}$

The translational angular momentum about $O$ is:
$L_{\text{trans}} = m v r_{\perp} = m v R$

The rotational angular momentum about the center of mass is:
$L_{\text{rot}} = I_{\text{cm}} \omega = \left(\dfrac{1}{2} m R^2\right) \left(\dfrac{v}{R}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2} m v R$

Since both components are in the same sense, they add up:
$L_O = m v R + \dfrac{1}{2} m v R = \dfrac{3}{2} m v R$

Comparing this with $\dfrac{x}{2} m v R$, we get $x = 3$.

Answer: $3$

questions.q: A uniform solid sphere of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is rotating freely about its diameter with an initial rotational kinetic energy $E$. Due to internal forces, the sphere collapses symmetrically such that its new radius becomes $\dfrac{R}{2}$, without any loss of mass. If the final rotational kinetic energy of the sphere is $xE$, the value of $x$ is
questions.question: A uniform solid sphere of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is rotating freely about its diameter with an initial rotational kinetic energy $E$. Due to internal forces, the sphere collapses symmetrically such that its new radius becomes $\dfrac{R}{2}$, without any loss of mass. If the final rotational kinetic energy of the sphere is $xE$, the value of $x$ is
questions.solution:
The initial moment of inertia of the solid sphere is:

$I_i = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2$

When the radius becomes $\dfrac{R}{2}$, the final moment of inertia is:

$I_f = \dfrac{2}{5}M\left(\dfrac{R}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{4}\left(\dfrac{2}{5}MR^2\right) = \dfrac{I_i}{4}$

Since no external torque acts on the sphere during the collapse, its angular momentum $L$ remains conserved.

The rotational kinetic energy is given by $K = \dfrac{L^2}{2I}$.

Since $L$ is constant, $K \propto \dfrac{1}{I}$.

Therefore, the final kinetic energy is:

$K_f = K_i \times \dfrac{I_i}{I_f} = E \times \dfrac{I_i}{\dfrac{I_i}{4}} = 4E$

Comparing this with $xE$, we get $x = 4$.

Answer: $4$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle of mass $2\text{ kg}$ moves such that its position vector as a function of time $t$ is given by $\vec{r}(t) = 2t^2\hat{i} + 3t\hat{j} + \hat{k}$, where $\vec{r}$ is in meters and $t$ is in seconds. The torque acting on the particle about the origin at $t = 2\text{ s}$ (in $\text{N m}$) is:
questions.question: A particle of mass $2\text{ kg}$ moves such that its position vector as a function of time $t$ is given by $\vec{r}(t) = 2t^2\hat{i} + 3t\hat{j} + \hat{k}$, where $\vec{r}$ is in meters and $t$ is in seconds. The torque acting on the particle about the origin at $t = 2\text{ s}$ (in $\text{N m}$) is:
questions.solution:
The position vector of the particle is $\vec{r}(t) = 2t^2\hat{i} + 3t\hat{j} + \hat{k}$.

Velocity is the first derivative of position with respect to time:

$\vec{v}(t) = \dfrac{d\vec{r}}{dt} = 4t\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}$

Acceleration is the derivative of velocity:

$\vec{a}(t) = \dfrac{d\vec{v}}{dt} = 4\hat{i}$

From Newton's Second Law, the force acting on the particle is:

$\vec{F} = m\vec{a} = 2(4\hat{i}) = 8\hat{i}\text{ N}$

At $t = 2\text{ s}$, the position vector is:

$\vec{r}(2) = 2(2)^2\hat{i} + 3(2)\hat{j} + \hat{k} = 8\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} + \hat{k}\text{ m}$

The torque about the origin is:

$\vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F} = (8\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} + \hat{k}) \times (8\hat{i})$

$\vec{\tau} = 8(\hat{i} \times \hat{i}) + 48(\hat{j} \times \hat{i}) + 8(\hat{k} \times \hat{i})$

Since $\hat{i} \times \hat{i} = 0$, $\hat{j} \times \hat{i} = -\hat{k}$, and $\hat{k} \times \hat{i} = \hat{j}$:

$\vec{\tau} = -48\hat{k} + 8\hat{j} = 8\hat{j} - 48\hat{k}\text{ N m}$

Answer: $8\hat{j} - 48\hat{k}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Four identical solid spheres, each of mass $2\text{ kg}$ and radius $10\text{ cm}$, are placed with their centers at the four corners of a square of side $50\text{ cm}$. The moment of inertia of the system about an axis passing through the center of the square and parallel to one of its sides is $x \times 10^{-3}\text{ kg m}^2$. The value of $x$ is ____.
questions.question: Four identical solid spheres, each of mass $2\text{ kg}$ and radius $10\text{ cm}$, are placed with their centers at the four corners of a square of side $50\text{ cm}$. The moment of inertia of the system about an axis passing through the center of the square and parallel to one of its sides is $x \times 10^{-3}\text{ kg m}^2$. The value of $x$ is ____.
questions.solution:
Let the mass of each sphere be $M = 2\text{ kg}$, radius $R = 10\text{ cm} = 0.1\text{ m}$, and the side of the square be $a = 50\text{ cm} = 0.5\text{ m}$.

The axis of rotation passes through the center of the square and is parallel to one of its sides. The perpendicular distance from the center of each of the four spheres to this axis is $d = \dfrac{a}{2} = 0.25\text{ m}$.

By the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia of one sphere about this axis is:
$I_1 = I_{\text{cm}} + Md^2 = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2 + M\left(\dfrac{a}{2}\right)^2$

Since there are four identical spheres at the same distance from the axis, the total moment of inertia of the system is:
$I = 4 \times I_1 = 4 \left[ \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2 + M\left(\dfrac{a}{2}\right)^2 \right]$

Substituting the given values:
$I = 4 \left[ \dfrac{2}{5}(2)(0.1)^2 + 2(0.25)^2 \right]$
$I = 4 \left[ 0.8 \times 0.01 + 2 \times 0.0625 \right]$
$I = 4 \left[ 0.008 + 0.125 \right]$
$I = 4 \times 0.133 = 0.532\text{ kg m}^2$

Expressing this in the required format:
$I = 532 \times 10^{-3}\text{ kg m}^2$

Thus, the value of $x$ is $532$.

Answer: $532$

questions.q: A uniform rod of mass $M$ and length $L$ is rotating freely with an angular velocity $\omega_0$ in a horizontal plane about a vertical axis passing through its center. Two small beads, each of mass $m$, are initially held at the center of the rod. The beads are then released and slide outwards along the rod until they reach the ends. The ratio of the final rotational kinetic energy to the initial rotational kinetic energy of the system is
questions.question: A uniform rod of mass $M$ and length $L$ is rotating freely with an angular velocity $\omega_0$ in a horizontal plane about a vertical axis passing through its center. Two small beads, each of mass $m$, are initially held at the center of the rod. The beads are then released and slide outwards along the rod until they reach the ends. The ratio of the final rotational kinetic energy to the initial rotational kinetic energy of the system is
questions.solution:
Since there is no external torque acting on the system, the angular momentum $L$ is conserved.

The rotational kinetic energy can be expressed in terms of angular momentum as $K = \dfrac{L^2}{2I}$.

Since $L$ is constant, the ratio of final to initial kinetic energy is $\dfrac{K_f}{K_i} = \dfrac{I_i}{I_f}$.

Initially, the beads are at the center, so their distance from the axis is zero. The initial moment of inertia is just that of the rod:
$I_i = \dfrac{ML^2}{12}$

Finally, the beads are at the ends of the rod, at a distance of $\dfrac{L}{2}$ from the axis. The final moment of inertia is:
$I_f = \dfrac{ML^2}{12} + 2 \times m \times \left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{ML^2}{12} + \dfrac{mL^2}{2}$

Taking the ratio:
$\dfrac{K_f}{K_i} = \dfrac{\dfrac{ML^2}{12}}{\dfrac{ML^2}{12} + \dfrac{mL^2}{2}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{M}{12}}{\dfrac{M + 6m}{12}} = \dfrac{M}{M+6m}$

Answer: $\dfrac{M}{M+6m}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform rolling body of radius $R$ is projected up an inclined plane with an initial speed $v$. It rolls without slipping and reaches a maximum vertical height $h = \dfrac{3v^2}{4g}$ before momentarily coming to rest. If the radius of gyration of the body about its center of mass is $k$, the value of $10 \left(\dfrac{k^2}{R^2}\right)$ is ______.
questions.question: A uniform rolling body of radius $R$ is projected up an inclined plane with an initial speed $v$. It rolls without slipping and reaches a maximum vertical height $h = \dfrac{3v^2}{4g}$ before momentarily coming to rest. If the radius of gyration of the body about its center of mass is $k$, the value of $10 \left(\dfrac{k^2}{R^2}\right)$ is ______.
questions.solution:
By the principle of conservation of mechanical energy, the total initial kinetic energy of the rolling body is converted into potential energy at the maximum height.

Loss in K.E. = Gain in P.E.

$\dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 \left(1 + \dfrac{k^2}{R^2}\right) = mgh$

Given that $h = \dfrac{3v^2}{4g}$, we substitute this into the equation:

$\dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 \left(1 + \dfrac{k^2}{R^2}\right) = mg \left(\dfrac{3v^2}{4g}\right)$

$\dfrac{1}{2} \left(1 + \dfrac{k^2}{R^2}\right) = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$1 + \dfrac{k^2}{R^2} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

$\dfrac{k^2}{R^2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Therefore, the value of $10 \left(\dfrac{k^2}{R^2}\right)$ is $10 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 5$.

Answer: $5$
