questions.q: A rigid cross is made of two identical uniform thin rods, each of mass $1.2 \text{ kg}$ and length $40 \text{ cm}$, joined at their centers at right angles. Four small point masses, each of mass $0.3 \text{ kg}$, are attached to the ends of the rods. The cross is mounted on a frictionless horizontal axle passing through its center. A light string is wrapped around a small cylindrical hub of radius $10 \text{ cm}$ fixed to the center of the cross, and a block of mass $2 \text{ kg}$ hangs from the free end of the string. If the system is released from rest, the angular acceleration of the cross is (Take $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.question: A rigid cross is made of two identical uniform thin rods, each of mass $1.2 \text{ kg}$ and length $40 \text{ cm}$, joined at their centers at right angles. Four small point masses, each of mass $0.3 \text{ kg}$, are attached to the ends of the rods. The cross is mounted on a frictionless horizontal axle passing through its center. A light string is wrapped around a small cylindrical hub of radius $10 \text{ cm}$ fixed to the center of the cross, and a block of mass $2 \text{ kg}$ hangs from the free end of the string. If the system is released from rest, the angular acceleration of the cross is (Take $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
Moment of inertia of the two rods about the central axis:
$I_{\text{rods}} = 2 \times \left(\dfrac{1}{12}M_{\text{r}}L^2\right) = 2 \times \dfrac{1}{12} \times 1.2 \times (0.4)^2 = 0.032 \text{ kg m}^2$.

Moment of inertia of the four point masses at distance $L/2$:
$I_{\text{masses}} = 4 \times m \left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right)^2 = 4 \times 0.3 \times (0.2)^2 = 0.048 \text{ kg m}^2$.

Total moment of inertia of the cross, $I = I_{\text{rods}} + I_{\text{masses}} = 0.032 + 0.048 = 0.08 \text{ kg m}^2$.

Let $T$ be the tension in the string and $a$ be the downward acceleration of the block.
Equation of motion for the block: $M_{\text{b}}g - T = M_{\text{b}}a$
Equation of motion for the cross: $TR_{\text{h}} = I\alpha$
Kinematic constraint: $a = \alpha R_{\text{h}}$

Substituting $a$ and $T$:
$M_{\text{b}}g - \dfrac{I\alpha}{R_{\text{h}}} = M_{\text{b}}(\alpha R_{\text{h}})$
$\alpha = \dfrac{M_{\text{b}}g}{M_{\text{b}}R_{\text{h}} + \dfrac{I}{R_{\text{h}}}} = \dfrac{M_{\text{b}}g R_{\text{h}}}{I + M_{\text{b}}R_{\text{h}}^2}$

Substituting the values:
$\alpha = \dfrac{2 \times 10 \times 0.1}{0.08 + 2 \times (0.1)^2} = \dfrac{2}{0.08 + 0.02} = \dfrac{2}{0.10} = 20 \text{ rad/s}^2$.

Answer: $20 \text{ rad/s}^2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Four identical solid spheres, each of mass $5 \text{ kg}$ and radius $1 \text{ m}$, are placed such that their centers lie exactly on the four corners of a square of side length $2 \text{ m}$. The total moment of inertia of this system about an axis passing through the center of the square and perpendicular to its plane is $\ldots\ldots \text{ kg m}^2$.
questions.question: Four identical solid spheres, each of mass $5 \text{ kg}$ and radius $1 \text{ m}$, are placed such that their centers lie exactly on the four corners of a square of side length $2 \text{ m}$. The total moment of inertia of this system about an axis passing through the center of the square and perpendicular to its plane is $\ldots\ldots \text{ kg m}^2$.
questions.solution:
The distance $d$ from the center of the square to any of its corners is half the length of the diagonal.

$d = \dfrac{a}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2} \text{ m}$

Using the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia of one solid sphere about the central axis is the sum of its moment of inertia about its own centroidal axis and the product of its mass and the square of the distance to the central axis.

$I_1 = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2 + Md^2$

$I_1 = \dfrac{2}{5}(5)(1)^2 + 5(\sqrt{2})^2$

$I_1 = 2 + 5(2) = 12 \text{ kg m}^2$

Since there are four identical spheres symmetrically placed, the total moment of inertia of the system is:

$I_{\text{total}} = 4 \times I_1 = 4 \times 12 = 48 \text{ kg m}^2$

Answer: $48$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform solid cone of base radius $R$ and height $H$ has a moment of inertia $I_{1}$ about its central axis of symmetry. A smaller solid cone of base radius $R / 3$ and height $H / 3$ is carved out from the top of this cone. The moment of inertia of this smaller cone about the same central axis is $I_{2}$. The ratio $\dfrac{I_{1}}{I_{2}}$ is ________.
questions.question: A uniform solid cone of base radius $R$ and height $H$ has a moment of inertia $I_{1}$ about its central axis of symmetry. A smaller solid cone of base radius $R / 3$ and height $H / 3$ is carved out from the top of this cone. The moment of inertia of this smaller cone about the same central axis is $I_{2}$. The ratio $\dfrac{I_{1}}{I_{2}}$ is ________.
questions.solution:
The moment of inertia of a uniform solid cone of mass $M$ and base radius $R$ about its central axis is $I = \dfrac{3}{10}MR^2$.

Since the mass of the cone is $M = \rho \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\pi R^2 H\right)$, the moment of inertia can be written as:
$I = \dfrac{3}{10} \left(\rho \dfrac{1}{3}\pi R^2 H\right) R^2 = \dfrac{1}{10}\rho \pi R^4 H$

For the original large cone:
$I_{1} = \dfrac{1}{10}\rho \pi R^4 H$

For the smaller carved-out cone, the base radius is $R/3$ and the height is $H/3$. Its moment of inertia about the same central axis is:
$I_{2} = \dfrac{1}{10}\rho \pi \left(\dfrac{R}{3}\right)^4 \left(\dfrac{H}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{10}\rho \pi \dfrac{R^4}{81} \dfrac{H}{3} = \dfrac{1}{243} \left(\dfrac{1}{10}\rho \pi R^4 H\right)$

Thus, $I_{2} = \dfrac{I_{1}}{243}$, which gives $\dfrac{I_{1}}{I_{2}} = 243$.

Answer: $243$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two identical thin circular rings, each of mass $3\text{ kg}$ and radius $R$, are fixed at the ends of a light rod of length $40\text{ cm}$. The centers of the rings are attached to the ends of the rod, and the planes of the rings are perpendicular to the rod. The moment of inertia of the system about an axis passing through the midpoint of the rod and perpendicular to it is $360 \times 10^{-3}\text{ kg m}^2$. The value of $R$ is ____ cm.
questions.question: Two identical thin circular rings, each of mass $3\text{ kg}$ and radius $R$, are fixed at the ends of a light rod of length $40\text{ cm}$. The centers of the rings are attached to the ends of the rod, and the planes of the rings are perpendicular to the rod. The moment of inertia of the system about an axis passing through the midpoint of the rod and perpendicular to it is $360 \times 10^{-3}\text{ kg m}^2$. The value of $R$ is ____ cm.
questions.solution:
Let the mass of each ring be $M = 3\text{ kg}$ and the length of the rod be $L = 40\text{ cm} = 0.4\text{ m}$.

The axis of rotation passes through the midpoint of the rod and is perpendicular to it. Since the planes of the rings are perpendicular to the rod, the axis of rotation is parallel to the planes of the rings (i.e., parallel to their diameters).

The distance from the center of each ring to the axis of rotation is $d = \dfrac{L}{2} = 0.2\text{ m}$.

By the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia of one ring about this axis is:
$I_1 = I_{\text{diameter}} + Md^2 = \dfrac{MR^2}{2} + M\left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right)^2$

The total moment of inertia of the system is:
$I = 2 I_1 = 2 \left[ \dfrac{MR^2}{2} + M\left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right)^2 \right] = MR^2 + \dfrac{ML^2}{2}$

Given $I = 360 \times 10^{-3}\text{ kg m}^2 = 0.36\text{ kg m}^2$, we substitute the known values:
$0.36 = 3R^2 + \dfrac{3 \times (0.4)^2}{2}$
$0.36 = 3R^2 + \dfrac{3 \times 0.16}{2}$
$0.36 = 3R^2 + 0.24$
$3R^2 = 0.12$
$R^2 = 0.04\text{ m}^2$
$R = 0.2\text{ m} = 20\text{ cm}$

Answer: $20$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two solid discs, A and B, are made of the same material. Disc A has radius $R$ and thickness $t$. Disc B has radius $3R$ and thickness $\dfrac{t}{3}$. Identical constant tangential forces $F$ are applied to the rim of each disc, causing them to rotate about their respective central axes. If the ratio of the angular acceleration of disc A to that of disc B is $x$, then the value of $x$ is ____.
questions.question: Two solid discs, A and B, are made of the same material. Disc A has radius $R$ and thickness $t$. Disc B has radius $3R$ and thickness $\dfrac{t}{3}$. Identical constant tangential forces $F$ are applied to the rim of each disc, causing them to rotate about their respective central axes. If the ratio of the angular acceleration of disc A to that of disc B is $x$, then the value of $x$ is ____.
questions.solution:
Let the density of the material be $\rho$.

The moment of inertia of a solid disc is $I = \dfrac{1}{2}MR^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}(\rho \pi R^2 t)R^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}\rho \pi R^4 t$.
For disc A: $I_A = \dfrac{1}{2}\rho \pi R^4 t$
For disc B: $I_B = \dfrac{1}{2}\rho \pi (3R)^4 \left(\dfrac{t}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\rho \pi (81R^4)\left(\dfrac{t}{3}\right) = 27 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\rho \pi R^4 t\right) = 27 I_A$

The torque produced by the tangential force $F$ is $\tau = F \times \text{radius}$.
For disc A: $\tau_A = F R$
For disc B: $\tau_B = F (3R) = 3 \tau_A$

Using Newton's second law for rotation, $\alpha = \dfrac{\tau}{I}$:
For disc A: $\alpha_A = \dfrac{\tau_A}{I_A}$
For disc B: $\alpha_B = \dfrac{\tau_B}{I_B} = \dfrac{3 \tau_A}{27 I_A} = \dfrac{1}{9} \alpha_A$

The ratio of their angular accelerations is:
$\dfrac{\alpha_A}{\alpha_B} = 9$

Thus, $x = 9$.

Answer: $9$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A string is wrapped around a uniform solid cylinder of mass $4\text{ kg}$ and radius $0.5\text{ m}$ which is free to rotate about its fixed central axis. Starting from rest at $t = 0$, a time-varying pulling force $F = (24t - 12t^2)\text{ N}$ is applied to the free end of the string, where $t$ is in seconds. The average power (in $\text{W}$) delivered by the force over the time interval from $t = 0$ until the angular acceleration of the cylinder becomes zero for the first time is ______.
questions.question: A string is wrapped around a uniform solid cylinder of mass $4\text{ kg}$ and radius $0.5\text{ m}$ which is free to rotate about its fixed central axis. Starting from rest at $t = 0$, a time-varying pulling force $F = (24t - 12t^2)\text{ N}$ is applied to the free end of the string, where $t$ is in seconds. The average power (in $\text{W}$) delivered by the force over the time interval from $t = 0$ until the angular acceleration of the cylinder becomes zero for the first time is ______.
questions.solution:
Torque applied on the cylinder is $\tau = F \times R = (24t - 12t^2)(0.5) = 12t - 6t^2\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$.

Moment of inertia of the solid cylinder is $I = \dfrac{1}{2}MR^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}(4)(0.5)^2 = 0.5\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2$.

Angular acceleration $\alpha = \dfrac{\tau}{I} = \dfrac{12t - 6t^2}{0.5} = 24t - 12t^2$.

The angular acceleration becomes zero when $\alpha = 0 \Rightarrow 24t - 12t^2 = 0 \Rightarrow t = 2\text{ s}$.

Angular velocity $\omega(t) = \int_0^t \alpha dt = \int_0^t (24t - 12t^2) dt = 12t^2 - 4t^3$.

At $t = 2\text{ s}$, the angular velocity is $\omega(2) = 12(2)^2 - 4(2)^3 = 48 - 32 = 16\text{ rad/s}$.

By the work-energy theorem, the total work done by the force is equal to the change in rotational kinetic energy:
$W = \Delta K = \dfrac{1}{2}I\omega^2 - 0 = \dfrac{1}{2}(0.5)(16)^2 = 64\text{ J}$.

The average power delivered over this time interval is $P_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{W}{\Delta t} = \dfrac{64}{2} = 32\text{ W}$.

Answer: $32$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle of mass $3 \text{ kg}$ is located at a position vector $\vec{r} = (2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 3\hat{k}) \text{ m}$. Its velocity vector is given by $\vec{v} = (\alpha\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}) \text{ m s}^{-1}$, where $\alpha$ is a constant. If the $y$-component and the $z$-component of the particle's angular momentum about the origin are equal in magnitude and sign, the value of $\alpha$ is
questions.question: A particle of mass $3 \text{ kg}$ is located at a position vector $\vec{r} = (2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 3\hat{k}) \text{ m}$. Its velocity vector is given by $\vec{v} = (\alpha\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}) \text{ m s}^{-1}$, where $\alpha$ is a constant. If the $y$-component and the $z$-component of the particle's angular momentum about the origin are equal in magnitude and sign, the value of $\alpha$ is
questions.solution:
The angular momentum of the particle about the origin is given by $\vec{L} = m(\vec{r} \times \vec{v})$.

First, we compute the cross product $\vec{r} \times \vec{v}$:
$\vec{r} \times \vec{v} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & -1 & 3 \\ \alpha & 2 & 1 \end{vmatrix}$

Expanding the determinant:
$\vec{r} \times \vec{v} = \hat{i}(-1 \times 1 - 3 \times 2) - \hat{j}(2 \times 1 - 3 \times \alpha) + \hat{k}(2 \times 2 - (-1) \times \alpha)$
$\vec{r} \times \vec{v} = -7\hat{i} + (3\alpha - 2)\hat{j} + (4 + \alpha)\hat{k}$

Multiplying by the mass $m = 3 \text{ kg}$:
$\vec{L} = -21\hat{i} + 3(3\alpha - 2)\hat{j} + 3(4 + \alpha)\hat{k}$

The $y$-component of the angular momentum is $L_y = 3(3\alpha - 2)$.
The $z$-component of the angular momentum is $L_z = 3(4 + \alpha)$.

Given that $L_y = L_z$:
$3(3\alpha - 2) = 3(4 + \alpha)$
$3\alpha - 2 = 4 + \alpha$
$2\alpha = 6$
$\alpha = 3$

Answer: $3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A wheel of radius $0.5$ m rolls without slipping on a horizontal surface, starting from rest. If the linear distance traveled by its center of mass in the first second is $\pi$ m, the number of revolutions made by the wheel during the $3^{\text{rd}}$ second of its motion is :
questions.question: A wheel of radius $0.5$ m rolls without slipping on a horizontal surface, starting from rest. If the linear distance traveled by its center of mass in the first second is $\pi$ m, the number of revolutions made by the wheel during the $3^{\text{rd}}$ second of its motion is :
questions.solution:
Let the linear acceleration of the center of mass be $a$.

The linear distance covered in the first second ($t = 1$ s) is:
$s = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}at^2$
$\pi = 0 + \dfrac{1}{2}a(1)^2$
$a = 2\pi \text{ m/s}^2$

For rolling without slipping, the angular acceleration $\alpha$ is:
$\alpha = \dfrac{a}{R} = \dfrac{2\pi}{0.5} = 4\pi \text{ rad/s}^2$

The angular displacement during the $3^{\text{rd}}$ second ($n = 3$) is:
$\Delta\theta = \omega_0 + \dfrac{\alpha}{2}(2n - 1)$
$\Delta\theta = 0 + \dfrac{4\pi}{2}(2(3) - 1)$
$\Delta\theta = 2\pi \times 5 = 10\pi \text{ rad}$

The number of revolutions made during the $3^{\text{rd}}$ second is:
$N = \dfrac{\Delta\theta}{2\pi} = \dfrac{10\pi}{2\pi} = 5$

Answer: $5$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform solid cylinder of radius $R$ and length $L$ has a moment of inertia $I_{0}$ about its central axis. A cylindrical portion of radius $R / 3$ and length $L$, whose axis is parallel to the central axis and at a distance of $2R / 3$ from it, is considered. The moment of inertia of this specific portion about the original central axis is $I_{p}$. The ratio $\dfrac{I_{0}}{I_{p}}$ is ________.
questions.question: A uniform solid cylinder of radius $R$ and length $L$ has a moment of inertia $I_{0}$ about its central axis. A cylindrical portion of radius $R / 3$ and length $L$, whose axis is parallel to the central axis and at a distance of $2R / 3$ from it, is considered. The moment of inertia of this specific portion about the original central axis is $I_{p}$. The ratio $\dfrac{I_{0}}{I_{p}}$ is ________.
questions.solution:
Let the mass of the original solid cylinder be $M$. Its moment of inertia about the central axis is $I_{0} = \dfrac{1}{2}MR^2$.

The considered cylindrical portion has the same length but a radius of $R/3$. Since mass is proportional to the square of the radius for a given length and uniform density, the mass of this portion is $m_{p} = M \times \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^2 = \dfrac{M}{9}$.

The moment of inertia of this portion about its own central axis is:
$I_{cm} = \dfrac{1}{2}m_{p}\left(\dfrac{R}{3}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{M}{9}\right)\dfrac{R^2}{9} = \dfrac{MR^2}{162}$

The axis of this portion is parallel to the original central axis and at a distance $d = 2R/3$. Using the parallel axis theorem, its moment of inertia about the original central axis is:
$I_{p} = I_{cm} + m_{p}d^2$
$I_{p} = \dfrac{MR^2}{162} + \left(\dfrac{M}{9}\right)\left(\dfrac{2R}{3}\right)^2 = \dfrac{MR^2}{162} + \dfrac{4MR^2}{81} = \dfrac{9MR^2}{162} = \dfrac{MR^2}{18}$

The ratio is $\dfrac{I_{0}}{I_{p}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}MR^2}{\dfrac{1}{18}MR^2} = 9$.

Answer: $9$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform solid cylinder of mass $2\text{ kg}$ and radius $10\text{ cm}$ is rotated about its central geometric axis with an angular speed of $5\text{ rad s}^{-1}$. If the moment of inertia of the cylinder about a generator (a line on the surface parallel to the central axis) is numerically equal to $x \times 10^{-1}$ times its angular momentum about the central axis, then the value of $x$ is
questions.question: A uniform solid cylinder of mass $2\text{ kg}$ and radius $10\text{ cm}$ is rotated about its central geometric axis with an angular speed of $5\text{ rad s}^{-1}$. If the moment of inertia of the cylinder about a generator (a line on the surface parallel to the central axis) is numerically equal to $x \times 10^{-1}$ times its angular momentum about the central axis, then the value of $x$ is
questions.solution:
The moment of inertia of a solid cylinder about its central axis is
$I_{\text{central}} = \dfrac{1}{2}MR^2$

The angular momentum about the central axis is
$L = I_{\text{central}}\omega = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}MR^2\right) \times 5 = \dfrac{5}{2}MR^2$

Using the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia about a generator (a line on the surface parallel to the central axis at a distance $R$) is
$I_{\text{gen}} = I_{\text{central}} + MR^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}MR^2 + MR^2 = \dfrac{3}{2}MR^2$

According to the given condition,
$I_{\text{gen}} = x \times 10^{-1} \times L$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{3}{2}MR^2 = \dfrac{x}{10} \times \dfrac{5}{2}MR^2$
$\Rightarrow 3 = \dfrac{x}{10} \times 5$
$\Rightarrow x = 6$

Answer: $6$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A projectile of mass $2 \text{ kg}$ is launched from a point on the $y$-axis with an initial position vector $\vec{r}_0 = 10\hat{j} \text{ m}$. Its initial velocity is $\vec{u} = (15\hat{i} + 20\hat{j}) \text{ m s}^{-1}$. Taking the acceleration due to gravity as $g = 10 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ along the negative $y$-axis, the magnitude of the angular momentum of the projectile about the origin at the instant it reaches its maximum height is (in $\text{N m s}$)
questions.question: A projectile of mass $2 \text{ kg}$ is launched from a point on the $y$-axis with an initial position vector $\vec{r}_0 = 10\hat{j} \text{ m}$. Its initial velocity is $\vec{u} = (15\hat{i} + 20\hat{j}) \text{ m s}^{-1}$. Taking the acceleration due to gravity as $g = 10 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ along the negative $y$-axis, the magnitude of the angular momentum of the projectile about the origin at the instant it reaches its maximum height is (in $\text{N m s}$)
questions.solution:
The projectile reaches its maximum height when its vertical velocity component becomes zero.
Using the first equation of motion for the $y$-direction:
$v_y = u_y - gt$
$0 = 20 - 10t \implies t = 2 \text{ s}$

At $t = 2 \text{ s}$, the position of the projectile is:
$x = u_x t = 15 \times 2 = 30 \text{ m}$
$y = y_0 + u_y t - \dfrac{1}{2}gt^2 = 10 + 20(2) - \dfrac{1}{2}(10)(2)^2 = 10 + 40 - 20 = 30 \text{ m}$
So, the position vector at maximum height is $\vec{r} = (30\hat{i} + 30\hat{j}) \text{ m}$.

At maximum height, the velocity vector has only the horizontal component:
$\vec{v} = v_x\hat{i} = 15\hat{i} \text{ m s}^{-1}$

The angular momentum about the origin is $\vec{L} = m(\vec{r} \times \vec{v})$.
$\vec{L} = 2 \left[ (30\hat{i} + 30\hat{j}) \times (15\hat{i}) \right]$
$\vec{L} = 2 \left[ 30 \times 15 (\hat{i} \times \hat{i}) + 30 \times 15 (\hat{j} \times \hat{i}) \right]$
Since $\hat{i} \times \hat{i} = 0$ and $\hat{j} \times \hat{i} = -\hat{k}$:
$\vec{L} = 2 \left[ 450(-\hat{k}) \right] = -900\hat{k} \text{ N m s}$

The magnitude of the angular momentum is $|\vec{L}| = 900 \text{ N m s}$.

Answer: $900$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solid sphere of mass $2\text{ kg}$ and radius $0.5\text{ m}$ is initially at rest. It is subjected to a time-varying torque $\tau = (0.8\pi t - \beta t^2)\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$ about its diameter, where $t$ is in seconds and $\beta$ is a positive constant. The sphere makes exactly $18$ rotations before its angular velocity becomes zero for the first time. The value of $\dfrac{10\beta}{\pi}$ is ______.
questions.question: A solid sphere of mass $2\text{ kg}$ and radius $0.5\text{ m}$ is initially at rest. It is subjected to a time-varying torque $\tau = (0.8\pi t - \beta t^2)\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$ about its diameter, where $t$ is in seconds and $\beta$ is a positive constant. The sphere makes exactly $18$ rotations before its angular velocity becomes zero for the first time. The value of $\dfrac{10\beta}{\pi}$ is ______.
questions.solution:
Moment of inertia of the solid sphere about its diameter is $I = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2 = \dfrac{2}{5}(2)(0.5)^2 = 0.2\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2$.

Angular acceleration $\alpha = \dfrac{\tau}{I} = \dfrac{0.8\pi t - \beta t^2}{0.2} = 4\pi t - 5\beta t^2$.

Angular velocity $\omega(t) = \int_0^t \alpha dt = 2\pi t^2 - \dfrac{5\beta}{3}t^3$.

The sphere reverses direction when $\omega(t) = 0$.
$2\pi t^2 - \dfrac{5\beta}{3}t^3 = 0 \Rightarrow t = \dfrac{6\pi}{5\beta}$.

Angular displacement $\theta(t) = \int_0^t \omega dt = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}t^3 - \dfrac{5\beta}{12}t^4$.

At the turning point $t = \dfrac{6\pi}{5\beta}$,
$\theta = \left(\dfrac{6\pi}{5\beta}\right)^3 \left[ \dfrac{2\pi}{3} - \dfrac{5\beta}{12} \left(\dfrac{6\pi}{5\beta}\right) \right] = \left(\dfrac{6\pi}{5\beta}\right)^3 \left( \dfrac{2\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{2} \right) = \left(\dfrac{6\pi}{5\beta}\right)^3 \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

Given the sphere makes $18$ rotations, $\theta = 18 \times 2\pi = 36\pi\text{ rad}$.

Equating the two expressions for $\theta$:
$\left(\dfrac{6\pi}{5\beta}\right)^3 \dfrac{\pi}{6} = 36\pi \Rightarrow \left(\dfrac{6\pi}{5\beta}\right)^3 = 216 \Rightarrow \dfrac{6\pi}{5\beta} = 6$.

Solving for $\beta$, we get $\beta = \dfrac{\pi}{5}$.

The value of $\dfrac{10\beta}{\pi} = \dfrac{10(\pi/5)}{\pi} = 2$.

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solid sphere of radius $R$ and a solid cylinder of radius $R$ and length $L$ are made of the same material. If they have equal moments of inertia about their respective central axes of symmetry, the length $L$ can be expressed as $L = \dfrac{x}{15}R$. The value of $x$ is ____.
questions.question: A solid sphere of radius $R$ and a solid cylinder of radius $R$ and length $L$ are made of the same material. If they have equal moments of inertia about their respective central axes of symmetry, the length $L$ can be expressed as $L = \dfrac{x}{15}R$. The value of $x$ is ____.
questions.solution:
Let the density of the material be $\rho$.

For the solid sphere, the mass is $M_s = \rho \left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3\right)$.
The moment of inertia about its central axis is:
$I_s = \dfrac{2}{5}M_s R^2 = \dfrac{2}{5}\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi \rho R^3\right)R^2 = \dfrac{8}{15}\pi \rho R^5$

For the solid cylinder, the mass is $M_c = \rho (\pi R^2 L)$.
The moment of inertia about its central axis is:
$I_c = \dfrac{1}{2}M_c R^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}(\pi \rho R^2 L)R^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}\pi \rho R^4 L$

Given that $I_s = I_c$:
$\dfrac{8}{15}\pi \rho R^5 = \dfrac{1}{2}\pi \rho R^4 L$

Cancelling common terms:
$\dfrac{8}{15}R = \dfrac{1}{2}L$
$L = \dfrac{16}{15}R$

Comparing this with $L = \dfrac{x}{15}R$, we get $x = 16$.

Answer: $16$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A composite rigid body consists of a thin uniform rod of mass $M$ and length $12\text{ cm}$, and two identical uniform solid spheres, each of mass $M$ and radius $15\text{ cm}$. The centres of the spheres are attached to the two ends of the rod. The system rotates about an axis passing through the midpoint of the rod and perpendicular to its length. If the radius of gyration of the entire system about this axis is $\sqrt{x}\text{ cm}$, the value of $x$ is _____.
questions.question: A composite rigid body consists of a thin uniform rod of mass $M$ and length $12\text{ cm}$, and two identical uniform solid spheres, each of mass $M$ and radius $15\text{ cm}$. The centres of the spheres are attached to the two ends of the rod. The system rotates about an axis passing through the midpoint of the rod and perpendicular to its length. If the radius of gyration of the entire system about this axis is $\sqrt{x}\text{ cm}$, the value of $x$ is _____.
questions.solution:
Let the axis of rotation be $YY'$.

The moment of inertia of the thin rod about an axis passing through its midpoint and perpendicular to its length is:

$I_{\text{rod}} = \dfrac{ML^2}{12} = \dfrac{M(12)^2}{12} = 12M$

For each solid sphere, the distance from its centre to the axis of rotation is $d = \dfrac{L}{2} = 6\text{ cm}$. By the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia of one sphere about the axis $YY'$ is:

$I_{\text{sphere}} = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2 + Md^2 = \dfrac{2}{5}M(15)^2 + M(6)^2$

$I_{\text{sphere}} = \dfrac{2}{5}M(225) + 36M = 90M + 36M = 126M$

The total moment of inertia of the composite system is:

$I_{\text{total}} = I_{\text{rod}} + 2I_{\text{sphere}} = 12M + 2(126M) = 264M$

The total mass of the system is $M_{\text{total}} = M + M + M = 3M$.

Let $k$ be the radius of gyration of the system. Then:

$I_{\text{total}} = M_{\text{total}}k^2$

$264M = (3M)k^2$

$k^2 = \dfrac{264}{3} = 88$

$k = \sqrt{88}\text{ cm}$

Comparing this with $\sqrt{x}\text{ cm}$, we get $x = 88$.

Answer: $88$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform solid sphere of radius $R$ has a moment of inertia $I_0$ about its diametric axis. A concentric spherical portion of radius $\dfrac{R}{2}$ is carved out of the original sphere. If $I_1$ is the moment of inertia of the remaining hollowed portion and $I_2$ is the moment of inertia of the carved out portion (both about the same diametric axis), then the ratio $\dfrac{I_1}{I_2}$ is __________.
questions.question: A uniform solid sphere of radius $R$ has a moment of inertia $I_0$ about its diametric axis. A concentric spherical portion of radius $\dfrac{R}{2}$ is carved out of the original sphere. If $I_1$ is the moment of inertia of the remaining hollowed portion and $I_2$ is the moment of inertia of the carved out portion (both about the same diametric axis), then the ratio $\dfrac{I_1}{I_2}$ is __________.
questions.solution:
The moment of inertia of a uniform solid sphere of radius $R$ and mass $M$ about its diametric axis is given by $I = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2$.

Since mass $M = \text{density} \times \text{volume} = \rho \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3$, we can express the moment of inertia in terms of density and radius as:
$I = \dfrac{2}{5} \left( \rho \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3 \right) R^2 = \dfrac{8}{15}\rho\pi R^5$

This shows that for a uniform sphere of constant density, the moment of inertia is proportional to the fifth power of its radius ($I \propto R^5$).

Let the moment of inertia of the original solid sphere be $I_0 = kR^5$, where $k = \dfrac{8}{15}\rho\pi$.

The moment of inertia of the carved out spherical portion of radius $\dfrac{R}{2}$ is:
$I_2 = k\left(\dfrac{R}{2}\right)^5 = \dfrac{kR^5}{32} = \dfrac{I_0}{32}$

The moment of inertia of the remaining hollowed portion is the difference between the original sphere and the carved out portion:
$I_1 = I_0 - I_2 = I_0 - \dfrac{I_0}{32} = \dfrac{31I_0}{32}$

The required ratio is:
$\dfrac{I_1}{I_2} = \dfrac{\dfrac{31I_0}{32}}{\dfrac{I_0}{32}} = 31$

Answer: $31$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform straight rod of length $L$ and a uniform solid disc of radius $R$ have the same radius of gyration. The rod rotates about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its length, while the disc rotates about one of its diameters. If the ratio of the length of the rod to the radius of the disc is $\sqrt{x}$, the value of $x$ is _____.
questions.question: A uniform straight rod of length $L$ and a uniform solid disc of radius $R$ have the same radius of gyration. The rod rotates about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its length, while the disc rotates about one of its diameters. If the ratio of the length of the rod to the radius of the disc is $\sqrt{x}$, the value of $x$ is _____.
questions.solution:
The moment of inertia of the rod about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its length is $I_{\text{rod}} = \dfrac{mL^2}{12}$.

Its radius of gyration squared is $k_{\text{rod}}^2 = \dfrac{L^2}{12}$.

The moment of inertia of the solid disc about its diameter is $I_{\text{disc}} = \dfrac{mR^2}{4}$.

Its radius of gyration squared is $k_{\text{disc}}^2 = \dfrac{R^2}{4}$.

Since the radii of gyration are equal:

$\dfrac{L^2}{12} = \dfrac{R^2}{4}$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{L^2}{R^2} = \dfrac{12}{4} = 3$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{L}{R} = \sqrt{3}$

Comparing this with $\sqrt{x}$, we get $x = 3$.

Answer: $3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle of mass $m$ is projected from the origin with an initial speed $u$ at an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal. The magnitude of the angular momentum of the particle about the point of its maximum height, evaluated at the exact instant the particle strikes the horizontal ground, is
questions.question: A particle of mass $m$ is projected from the origin with an initial speed $u$ at an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal. The magnitude of the angular momentum of the particle about the point of its maximum height, evaluated at the exact instant the particle strikes the horizontal ground, is
questions.solution:
Let the point of projection be the origin $(0,0)$.

The coordinates of the highest point $P$ are $\left( \dfrac{R}{2}, H \right) = \left( \dfrac{u^2 \sin 2\theta}{2g}, \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g} \right)$.

The coordinates of the landing point $Q$ are $(R, 0) = \left( \dfrac{u^2 \sin 2\theta}{g}, 0 \right)$.

The position vector of the landing point relative to the highest point is:
$\vec{r}' = \vec{r}_Q - \vec{r}_P = \left( R - \dfrac{R}{2} \right) \hat{i} + (0 - H) \hat{j} = \dfrac{R}{2} \hat{i} - H \hat{j}$.

At the instant of landing, the velocity vector of the particle is:
$\vec{v} = u \cos\theta \hat{i} - u \sin\theta \hat{j}$.

The angular momentum of the particle about the highest point is given by $\vec{L} = m (\vec{r}' \times \vec{v})$.

$\vec{r}' \times \vec{v} = \left( \dfrac{R}{2} \hat{i} - H \hat{j} \right) \times (u \cos\theta \hat{i} - u \sin\theta \hat{j})$
$= \dfrac{R}{2} (-u \sin\theta) \hat{k} - (-H) (u \cos\theta) (-\hat{k})$
$= \left( - \dfrac{R u \sin\theta}{2} + H u \cos\theta \right) \hat{k}$.

Substitute $R = \dfrac{2 u^2 \sin\theta \cos\theta}{g}$ and $H = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g}$:
$\vec{r}' \times \vec{v} = \left( - \dfrac{u^2 \sin\theta \cos\theta}{g} (u \sin\theta) + \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g} (u \cos\theta) \right) \hat{k}$
$= \left( - \dfrac{u^3 \sin^2\theta \cos\theta}{g} + \dfrac{u^3 \sin^2\theta \cos\theta}{2g} \right) \hat{k} = - \dfrac{u^3 \sin^2\theta \cos\theta}{2g} \hat{k}$.

The magnitude of the angular momentum is $|\vec{L}| = \dfrac{m u^3 \sin^2\theta \cos\theta}{2g}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{m u^3 \sin^2\theta \cos\theta}{2g}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform solid cylinder of radius $R$ and length $L$ has a moment of inertia $I_0$ about its central axis. A cylindrical hole of radius $r$ is drilled along its entire central axis. The moment of inertia of the resulting hollow cylinder about the same axis is found to be $\dfrac{80}{81}I_0$. The value of the ratio $\dfrac{R}{r}$ is __________.
questions.question: A uniform solid cylinder of radius $R$ and length $L$ has a moment of inertia $I_0$ about its central axis. A cylindrical hole of radius $r$ is drilled along its entire central axis. The moment of inertia of the resulting hollow cylinder about the same axis is found to be $\dfrac{80}{81}I_0$. The value of the ratio $\dfrac{R}{r}$ is __________.
questions.solution:
The moment of inertia of a uniform solid cylinder of radius $R$, length $L$, and mass $M$ about its central axis is $I = \dfrac{1}{2}MR^2$.

The mass of the cylinder is $M = \rho \times \pi R^2 L$.
Substituting this into the moment of inertia formula gives:
$I = \dfrac{1}{2}(\rho \pi R^2 L)R^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}\rho \pi L R^4$

Thus, for a cylinder of fixed length and constant density, the moment of inertia is proportional to the fourth power of its radius ($I \propto R^4$).

Let the moment of inertia of the original solid cylinder be $I_0 = kR^4$, where $k = \dfrac{1}{2}\rho \pi L$.

The moment of inertia of the cylindrical portion that was drilled out (which has radius $r$) is $I_{\text{hole}} = kr^4$.

The moment of inertia of the remaining hollow cylinder is:
$I_{\text{remaining}} = I_0 - I_{\text{hole}} = k(R^4 - r^4)$

We are given that $I_{\text{remaining}} = \dfrac{80}{81}I_0$.
Substituting the expressions, we get:
$k(R^4 - r^4) = \dfrac{80}{81}(kR^4)$

Dividing both sides by $k$:
$R^4 - r^4 = \dfrac{80}{81}R^4$

Rearranging the terms:
$r^4 = R^4 - \dfrac{80}{81}R^4 = \dfrac{1}{81}R^4$

Taking the fourth root of both sides:
$r = \dfrac{R}{3}$

Therefore, the ratio $\dfrac{R}{r} = 3$.

Answer: $3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solid cylinder of mass $M$ and radius $R$ rolls without slipping on a rough horizontal surface with a speed $v$. It then enters a smooth horizontal region and strikes a smooth vertical wall elastically. After rebounding from the wall, the cylinder eventually re-enters the rough horizontal surface. The final steady speed of the cylinder when pure rolling is re-established on the rough surface is:
questions.question: A solid cylinder of mass $M$ and radius $R$ rolls without slipping on a rough horizontal surface with a speed $v$. It then enters a smooth horizontal region and strikes a smooth vertical wall elastically. After rebounding from the wall, the cylinder eventually re-enters the rough horizontal surface. The final steady speed of the cylinder when pure rolling is re-established on the rough surface is:
questions.solution:
Let the initial velocity of the cylinder be $v$ towards the right. For pure rolling, its initial angular velocity is $\omega = \dfrac{v}{R}$ (clockwise).

When the cylinder enters the smooth region and strikes the smooth vertical wall elastically, its linear velocity reverses to $v$ towards the left. Since both the wall and the floor are smooth, no frictional torque acts on the cylinder. Thus, its angular velocity remains $\omega = \dfrac{v}{R}$ (clockwise).

When the cylinder re-enters the rough surface, it is moving to the left with speed $v$ but still rotating clockwise. Friction will act to oppose the slipping until pure rolling is re-established. During this process, the net torque about any point on the horizontal surface is zero, so angular momentum about a point on the surface is conserved.

Taking the leftward direction as positive for translation and counter-clockwise as positive for rotation:
Initial angular momentum about a point on the ground:
$L_i = MvR + I_{cm}(-\omega) = MvR - \left(\dfrac{1}{2}MR^2\right)\left(\dfrac{v}{R}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}MvR$

Let the final steady speed be $v_f$ (to the left). For pure rolling, the final angular velocity is $\omega_f = \dfrac{v_f}{R}$ (counter-clockwise).
Final angular momentum:
$L_f = Mv_fR + I_{cm}\omega_f = Mv_fR + \left(\dfrac{1}{2}MR^2\right)\left(\dfrac{v_f}{R}\right) = \dfrac{3}{2}Mv_fR$

Equating initial and final angular momentum:
$\dfrac{1}{2}MvR = \dfrac{3}{2}Mv_fR$

$\Rightarrow v_f = \dfrac{v}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{v}{3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A square loop is made of four identical uniform solid cylinders, each of mass $m$, radius $R$, and length $L$. The loop is hinged freely along the entire length of its top side (the longitudinal axis of the top cylinder) so that it can oscillate as a physical pendulum in a vertical plane. The time period of small oscillations of this square loop is :
questions.question: A square loop is made of four identical uniform solid cylinders, each of mass $m$, radius $R$, and length $L$. The loop is hinged freely along the entire length of its top side (the longitudinal axis of the top cylinder) so that it can oscillate as a physical pendulum in a vertical plane. The time period of small oscillations of this square loop is :
questions.solution:
To find the time period of the physical pendulum, we first calculate the moment of inertia of the square loop about the hinge axis (the longitudinal axis of the top cylinder).

1. Top cylinder (axis is its own longitudinal axis):
$I_{\text{top}} = \dfrac{1}{2} m R^{2}$

2. Bottom cylinder (parallel to the hinge axis at a distance $L$):
Using the parallel axis theorem:
$I_{\text{bottom}} = \dfrac{1}{2} m R^{2} + mL^{2}$

3. Two side cylinders (axis is perpendicular to their length and passes through one end):
For each side cylinder, $I = I_{\text{cm}} + m\left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right)^{2} = \left(\dfrac{m R^{2}}{4} + \dfrac{mL^{2}}{12}\right) + \dfrac{mL^{2}}{4} = \dfrac{m R^{2}}{4} + \dfrac{mL^{2}}{3}$
For both side cylinders combined:
$I_{\text{sides}} = 2 \times \left(\dfrac{m R^{2}}{4} + \dfrac{mL^{2}}{3}\right) = \dfrac{m R^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{2 mL^{2}}{3}$

Total moment of inertia about the hinge axis is:
$I_{\text{hinge}} = \dfrac{1}{2} m R^{2} + \left(\dfrac{1}{2} m R^{2} + mL^{2}\right) + \left(\dfrac{m R^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{2 mL^{2}}{3}\right) = \dfrac{3}{2} m R^{2} + \dfrac{5}{3} mL^{2}$

Next, we find the distance $d$ of the center of mass of the entire loop from the hinge axis. The top cylinder is at distance $0$, the two side cylinders have their centers at distance $\dfrac{L}{2}$, and the bottom cylinder is at distance $L$.
$d = \dfrac{m(0) + 2m\left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right) + m(L)}{4m} = \dfrac{2mL}{4m} = \dfrac{L}{2}$

The total mass is $M_{\text{tot}} = 4m$. The time period of a physical pendulum is given by:
$T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{I_{\text{hinge}}}{M_{\text{tot}} g d}}$

Substituting the values:
$T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{\dfrac{3}{2} m R^{2} + \dfrac{5}{3} mL^{2}}{4m \cdot g \cdot \dfrac{L}{2}}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{\dfrac{3}{2} R^{2} + \dfrac{5}{3} L^{2}}{2 g L}}$

Multiplying the numerator and denominator inside the square root by $6$ to clear the fractions:
$T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{9 R^{2} + 10 L^{2}}{12 g L}}$

Answer: $2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{9 R^{2} + 10 L^{2}}{12 g L}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform rigid body of circular cross-section (mass $m$, radius $R$) is rolling without slipping on a horizontal flat surface. The magnitude of its total angular momentum about a point on the surface in its path is $\dfrac{7}{5}$ times the magnitude of its translational angular momentum about the same point. The shape of the body is
questions.question: A uniform rigid body of circular cross-section (mass $m$, radius $R$) is rolling without slipping on a horizontal flat surface. The magnitude of its total angular momentum about a point on the surface in its path is $\dfrac{7}{5}$ times the magnitude of its translational angular momentum about the same point. The shape of the body is
questions.solution:
Let the moment of inertia of the body about its center of mass be $I_{\text{cm}}$.

For a body rolling without slipping with center of mass velocity $v$, its angular velocity is $\omega = \dfrac{v}{R}$.

The translational angular momentum of the body about a point on the surface is:
$L_{\text{trans}} = m v R = m (\omega R) R = m R^2 \omega$

The total angular momentum about the same point is the sum of translational and rotational angular momenta:
$L_{\text{total}} = L_{\text{trans}} + L_{\text{rot}} = m v R + I_{\text{cm}} \omega = m R^2 \omega + I_{\text{cm}} \omega$

According to the given condition:
$L_{\text{total}} = \dfrac{7}{5} L_{\text{trans}}$

Substituting the expressions, we get:
$m R^2 \omega + I_{\text{cm}} \omega = \dfrac{7}{5} m R^2 \omega$

$I_{\text{cm}} = \dfrac{7}{5} m R^2 - m R^2 = \dfrac{2}{5} m R^2$

The moment of inertia $\dfrac{2}{5} m R^2$ corresponds to a solid sphere.

Answer: Solid sphere

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle of mass $m$ moves in the $xy$-plane with its position vector at time $t$ given by $\vec{r}(t) = a \cos(\omega t) \hat{i} + b \sin(\omega t) \hat{j}$, where $a$ and $b$ are positive constants such that $a > b$. Which of the following statements is correct regarding the dynamics of the particle?
questions.question: A particle of mass $m$ moves in the $xy$-plane with its position vector at time $t$ given by $\vec{r}(t) = a \cos(\omega t) \hat{i} + b \sin(\omega t) \hat{j}$, where $a$ and $b$ are positive constants such that $a > b$. Which of the following statements is correct regarding the dynamics of the particle?
options: The force acting on the particle is not directed towards the origin.
The torque acting on the particle about the origin is non-zero, hence its angular momentum varies with time.
The angular momentum of the particle about the origin is conserved, but its kinetic energy varies with time.
Both the angular momentum about the origin and the kinetic energy of the particle remain constant.
questions.solution:
Given the position vector $\vec{r}(t) = a \cos(\omega t) \hat{i} + b \sin(\omega t) \hat{j}$.

Velocity of the particle:
$\vec{v}(t) = \dfrac{d\vec{r}}{dt} = -a\omega \sin(\omega t) \hat{i} + b\omega \cos(\omega t) \hat{j}$

Acceleration of the particle:
$\vec{a}(t) = \dfrac{d\vec{v}}{dt} = -a\omega^2 \cos(\omega t) \hat{i} - b\omega^2 \sin(\omega t) \hat{j} = -\omega^2 \vec{r}(t)$

The force acting on the particle is $\vec{F} = m\vec{a} = -m\omega^2 \vec{r}$. Since the force is always directed opposite to the position vector, it is a central force directed towards the origin.

The torque about the origin is $\vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F} = \vec{r} \times (-m\omega^2 \vec{r}) = 0$. Since the net torque is zero, the angular momentum of the particle about the origin is conserved.

The kinetic energy of the particle is $K = \dfrac{1}{2} m |\vec{v}|^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} m (a^2 \omega^2 \sin^2(\omega t) + b^2 \omega^2 \cos^2(\omega t))$.
Since $a \neq b$, the magnitude of velocity changes with time, meaning the kinetic energy is not constant.

Thus, the angular momentum is conserved, but the kinetic energy varies with time.

Answer: The angular momentum of the particle about the origin is conserved, but its kinetic energy varies with time.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform solid disc of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is rotating freely with an angular velocity $\omega_0$ about a vertical axis passing through its center. Two identical lumps of putty, each of mass $m$, are dropped gently onto the disc. They stick to the disc at a distance of $\dfrac{R}{2}$ from the axis of rotation, on opposite sides. The new angular velocity of the system is
questions.question: A uniform solid disc of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is rotating freely with an angular velocity $\omega_0$ about a vertical axis passing through its center. Two identical lumps of putty, each of mass $m$, are dropped gently onto the disc. They stick to the disc at a distance of $\dfrac{R}{2}$ from the axis of rotation, on opposite sides. The new angular velocity of the system is
questions.solution:
Since the lumps of putty are dropped gently, there is no external torque acting on the system about the axis of rotation. Therefore, angular momentum is conserved.

Initial moment of inertia of the solid disc is $I_i = \dfrac{1}{2}MR^2$

The two lumps of putty are placed at a distance of $\dfrac{R}{2}$ from the axis. Their combined moment of inertia is $I_{putty} = 2 \times m \times \left(\dfrac{R}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}mR^2$

Final moment of inertia of the system is $I_f = I_i + I_{putty} = \dfrac{1}{2}MR^2 + \dfrac{1}{2}mR^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}(M+m)R^2$

By conservation of angular momentum, $I_i \omega_0 = I_f \omega_f$

$\dfrac{1}{2}MR^2 \omega_0 = \dfrac{1}{2}(M+m)R^2 \omega_f$

$\omega_f = \dfrac{M}{M+m} \omega_0$

Answer: $\dfrac{M}{M+m} \omega_0$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform rod of length $120\text{ cm}$ and mass $300\text{ g}$ is supported on a knife-edge. A point mass of $150\text{ g}$ is attached to the $0\text{ cm}$ end of the rod. If the system is in horizontal equilibrium, the position of the knife-edge from the $0\text{ cm}$ end is ________ $\text{cm}$.
questions.question: A uniform rod of length $120\text{ cm}$ and mass $300\text{ g}$ is supported on a knife-edge. A point mass of $150\text{ g}$ is attached to the $0\text{ cm}$ end of the rod. If the system is in horizontal equilibrium, the position of the knife-edge from the $0\text{ cm}$ end is ________ $\text{cm}$.
questions.solution:
Let the knife-edge be at a distance $x\text{ cm}$ from the $0\text{ cm}$ end.

The mass of the uniform rod is $300\text{ g}$, and its weight acts at its geometric centre, which is at the $60\text{ cm}$ mark.

For rotational equilibrium about the knife-edge, the net torque must be zero.

Torque due to the $150\text{ g}$ mass = Torque due to the mass of the rod

$150g \times x = 300g \times (60 - x)$

$150x = 18000 - 300x$

$450x = 18000$

$x = 40$

The position of the knife-edge is $40\text{ cm}$ from the $0\text{ cm}$ end.

Answer: $40$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A block of mass $m = 1$ kg rests on top of a larger block of mass $M = 4$ kg. The larger block is placed on a smooth horizontal surface and is connected to a rigid wall by a horizontal spring of unknown spring constant $k$. The coefficient of static friction between the two blocks is $\mu = 0.5$. The system is set into simple harmonic motion. If the maximum kinetic energy of the system such that the upper block just avoids slipping is $1.25$ J, what is the value of the spring constant $k$? (Take $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.question: A block of mass $m = 1$ kg rests on top of a larger block of mass $M = 4$ kg. The larger block is placed on a smooth horizontal surface and is connected to a rigid wall by a horizontal spring of unknown spring constant $k$. The coefficient of static friction between the two blocks is $\mu = 0.5$. The system is set into simple harmonic motion. If the maximum kinetic energy of the system such that the upper block just avoids slipping is $1.25$ J, what is the value of the spring constant $k$? (Take $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
For the upper block not to slip, its maximum acceleration must not exceed the acceleration provided by limiting static friction.

The maximum frictional force on the upper block is:
$f_{\max} = \mu m g = 0.5 \times 1 \times 10 = 5 \text{ N}$

The maximum acceleration of the system is therefore:
$a_{\max} = \dfrac{f_{\max}}{m} = \dfrac{5}{1} = 5 \text{ m/s}^2$

The angular frequency of the two-block system is given by $\omega^2 = \dfrac{k}{M+m} = \dfrac{k}{5}$.

Using the relation for maximum acceleration in SHM, $a_{\max} = \omega^2 A$, we find the amplitude $A$:
$5 = \left(\dfrac{k}{5}\right) A \implies A = \dfrac{25}{k}$

The maximum kinetic energy of the system is given by $E = \dfrac{1}{2} k A^2$. Substituting the given value of $E$ and the expression for $A$:
$1.25 = \dfrac{1}{2} k \left(\dfrac{25}{k}\right)^2$
$1.25 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{625}{k}$
$1.25 = \dfrac{312.5}{k}$

Solving for $k$:
$k = \dfrac{312.5}{1.25} = 250 \text{ N/m}$

Answer: $250 \text{ N/m}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A hollow spherical shell of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is rolling without slipping on a rough horizontal floor with a constant speed $v$. It then enters a smooth horizontal section where it collides head-on with an ideal spring of force constant $k$ attached to a vertical wall. The maximum compression of the spring is:
questions.question: A hollow spherical shell of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is rolling without slipping on a rough horizontal floor with a constant speed $v$. It then enters a smooth horizontal section where it collides head-on with an ideal spring of force constant $k$ attached to a vertical wall. The maximum compression of the spring is:
questions.solution:
When the hollow spherical shell enters the smooth horizontal section, the frictional force becomes zero. Consequently, there is no external torque acting on the shell about its center of mass, and its angular velocity $\omega$ remains constant.

As the shell compresses the spring, the spring force acts horizontally through the center of mass, so it also produces no torque. Therefore, the rotational kinetic energy of the shell is conserved during the compression.

Only the translational kinetic energy of the shell is converted into the elastic potential energy of the spring. Applying conservation of mechanical energy for the translational motion:

$\dfrac{1}{2}Mv^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}kx^2$

$\Rightarrow x = v\sqrt{\dfrac{M}{k}}$

Answer: $v\sqrt{\dfrac{M}{k}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform ladder rests against a perfectly smooth vertical wall and a rough horizontal floor. It makes an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal floor and is on the verge of slipping. The minimum coefficient of static friction $\mu$ between the ladder and the floor is :
questions.question: A uniform ladder rests against a perfectly smooth vertical wall and a rough horizontal floor. It makes an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal floor and is on the verge of slipping. The minimum coefficient of static friction $\mu$ between the ladder and the floor is :
questions.solution:
Let the weight of the ladder be $W$ and its length be $L$.

For translational equilibrium, the normal reaction from the floor $N_{f}$ balances the weight of the ladder:
$N_{f} = W$

The normal reaction from the wall $N_{w}$ balances the static friction $f$ from the floor:
$f = N_{w}$

For rotational equilibrium, taking torque about the point of contact with the floor:
The weight $W$ acts at the center of the ladder, producing a torque $W \left( \dfrac{L}{2} \cos \theta \right)$.
The normal reaction from the wall $N_{w}$ produces an opposing torque $N_{w} (L \sin \theta)$.

Equating the torques:
$W \left( \dfrac{L}{2} \cos \theta \right) = N_{w} (L \sin \theta)$
$\Rightarrow N_{w} = \dfrac{W}{2} \cot \theta$

Since the ladder is on the verge of slipping, the friction is limiting:
$f = \mu N_{f}$

Substituting $f = N_{w}$ and $N_{f} = W$:
$\dfrac{W}{2} \cot \theta = \mu W$
$\Rightarrow \mu = \dfrac{1}{2} \cot \theta$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{2} \cot \theta$

questions.q: A rigid, massless L-shaped rod OAB is pivoted smoothly at the bend O. The arm OA has a length of $40 \text{ cm}$ and is held horizontally. The arm OB has a length of $20 \text{ cm}$ and extends vertically upwards from O. Three forces act on the rod to keep it in rotational equilibrium: a $50 \text{ N}$ force acts downwards at end A, a $25 \text{ N}$ force acts upwards at the exact midpoint of OA, and an unknown horizontal force $F$ acts to the left at end B. The magnitude of the force $F$ is :
questions.question: A rigid, massless L-shaped rod OAB is pivoted smoothly at the bend O. The arm OA has a length of $40 \text{ cm}$ and is held horizontally. The arm OB has a length of $20 \text{ cm}$ and extends vertically upwards from O. Three forces act on the rod to keep it in rotational equilibrium: a $50 \text{ N}$ force acts downwards at end A, a $25 \text{ N}$ force acts upwards at the exact midpoint of OA, and an unknown horizontal force $F$ acts to the left at end B. The magnitude of the force $F$ is :
questions.solution:
For the rod to be in rotational equilibrium, the net torque about the pivot O must be zero.

The force of $50 \text{ N}$ at A acts at a perpendicular distance of $40 \text{ cm} = 0.4 \text{ m}$ from O. It produces a clockwise torque:
$\tau_{1} = 50 \times 0.4 = 20 \text{ N m}$

The force of $25 \text{ N}$ at the midpoint of OA acts at a perpendicular distance of $20 \text{ cm} = 0.2 \text{ m}$ from O. It produces a counter-clockwise torque:
$\tau_{2} = 25 \times 0.2 = 5 \text{ N m}$

The force $F$ at B acts horizontally to the left at a perpendicular distance equal to the length of OB, which is $20 \text{ cm} = 0.2 \text{ m}$. It produces a counter-clockwise torque:
$\tau_{3} = F \times 0.2$

Equating the sum of counter-clockwise torques to the clockwise torque:
$\tau_{2} + \tau_{3} = \tau_{1}$
$5 + 0.2F = 20$
$0.2F = 15$
$F = \dfrac{15}{0.2} = 75 \text{ N}$

Answer: $75 \text{ N}$

questions.q: A particle is executing simple harmonic motion with an amplitude $A$. At a displacement of $\dfrac{A}{2}$ from the mean position, the potential energy of the particle is $12\text{ J}$. The maximum kinetic energy of the particle during its motion is
questions.question: A particle is executing simple harmonic motion with an amplitude $A$. At a displacement of $\dfrac{A}{2}$ from the mean position, the potential energy of the particle is $12\text{ J}$. The maximum kinetic energy of the particle during its motion is
questions.solution:
The potential energy of a particle executing simple harmonic motion at a displacement $x$ is given by $U = \dfrac{1}{2}m\omega^2 x^2$.

Given that at $x = \dfrac{A}{2}$, the potential energy is $12\text{ J}$:
$U = \dfrac{1}{2}m\omega^2 \left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{4} \left(\dfrac{1}{2}m\omega^2 A^2\right)$

Let the total mechanical energy (which is equal to the maximum kinetic energy) be $E = \dfrac{1}{2}m\omega^2 A^2$.

Therefore, $U = \dfrac{E}{4}$.

Given $U = 12\text{ J}$, we have:
$\dfrac{E}{4} = 12 \Rightarrow E = 48\text{ J}$

In simple harmonic motion, the maximum kinetic energy is equal to the total mechanical energy.
Thus, the maximum kinetic energy is $48\text{ J}$.

Answer: $48\text{ J}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform solid sphere of radius $R$ and a uniform thin spherical shell of radius $r$ both rotate about their respective tangential axes. If their radii of gyration about these axes are equal, the ratio $\dfrac{R^2}{r^2}$ can be expressed as $\dfrac{x}{21}$. The value of $x$ is ________.
questions.question: A uniform solid sphere of radius $R$ and a uniform thin spherical shell of radius $r$ both rotate about their respective tangential axes. If their radii of gyration about these axes are equal, the ratio $\dfrac{R^2}{r^2}$ can be expressed as $\dfrac{x}{21}$. The value of $x$ is ________.
questions.solution:
The radius of gyration $k$ of a body about an axis is given by $k^2 = \dfrac{I}{M}$.
For a uniform solid sphere about a tangential axis, using the parallel axis theorem:
$I_{solid} = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2 + MR^2 = \dfrac{7}{5}MR^2$
Thus, $k_{solid}^2 = \dfrac{7}{5}R^2$

For a uniform thin spherical shell (hollow sphere) about a tangential axis:
$I_{hollow} = \dfrac{2}{3}mr^2 + mr^2 = \dfrac{5}{3}mr^2$
Thus, $k_{hollow}^2 = \dfrac{5}{3}r^2$

Given that their radii of gyration are equal:
$k_{solid}^2 = k_{hollow}^2$
$\dfrac{7}{5}R^2 = \dfrac{5}{3}r^2$
$\dfrac{R^2}{r^2} = \dfrac{25}{21}$

Comparing this with $\dfrac{x}{21}$, we get $x = 25$.

Answer: $25$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A horizontal uniform circular disc of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is rotating freely about a frictionless vertical axis passing through its centre. A person of mass $m$ is standing at the edge of the disc. The initial rotational kinetic energy of the system is $E$. The person slowly walks towards the centre of the disc and stops. If $M = 4m$, the work done by the person in walking to the centre is $\dfrac{E}{x}$. The value of $x$ is
questions.question: A horizontal uniform circular disc of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is rotating freely about a frictionless vertical axis passing through its centre. A person of mass $m$ is standing at the edge of the disc. The initial rotational kinetic energy of the system is $E$. The person slowly walks towards the centre of the disc and stops. If $M = 4m$, the work done by the person in walking to the centre is $\dfrac{E}{x}$. The value of $x$ is
questions.solution:
The initial moment of inertia of the system (disc + person at the edge) is:

$I_i = \dfrac{1}{2}MR^2 + mR^2$

Given $M = 4m$, we have:

$I_i = \dfrac{1}{2}(4m)R^2 + mR^2 = 2mR^2 + mR^2 = 3mR^2$

When the person reaches the centre, their distance from the axis of rotation is zero. The final moment of inertia of the system is:

$I_f = \dfrac{1}{2}MR^2 + 0 = 2mR^2$

Since no external torque acts on the system, the angular momentum $L$ is conserved.

The final kinetic energy is related to the initial kinetic energy by:

$K_f = \dfrac{L^2}{2I_f} = K_i \times \dfrac{I_i}{I_f}$

$K_f = E \times \left(\dfrac{3mR^2}{2mR^2}\right) = \dfrac{3E}{2}$

According to the work-energy theorem, the work done by the internal forces (the person walking) is equal to the change in the rotational kinetic energy of the system:

$W = K_f - K_i = \dfrac{3E}{2} - E = \dfrac{E}{2}$

Comparing this with $\dfrac{E}{x}$, we get $x = 2$.

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A force $\vec{F} = \alpha\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$ acts on a particle whose position vector is $\vec{r} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$. If the torque acting on the particle about the origin is $\vec{\tau} = -10\hat{i} + 12\hat{j} + 8\hat{k}$, the value of $\alpha$ is:
questions.question: A force $\vec{F} = \alpha\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$ acts on a particle whose position vector is $\vec{r} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$. If the torque acting on the particle about the origin is $\vec{\tau} = -10\hat{i} + 12\hat{j} + 8\hat{k}$, the value of $\alpha$ is:
questions.solution:
The torque is given by the cross product of the position vector and the force vector:

$\vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F}$

$\vec{\tau} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & -1 & 4 \\ \alpha & 3 & -2 \end{vmatrix}$

Expanding the determinant:

$\vec{\tau} = \hat{i}[(-1)(-2) - (4)(3)] - \hat{j}[(2)(-2) - (4)(\alpha)] + \hat{k}[(2)(3) - (-1)(\alpha)]$

$\vec{\tau} = -10\hat{i} + (4 + 4\alpha)\hat{j} + (6 + \alpha)\hat{k}$

We are given that $\vec{\tau} = -10\hat{i} + 12\hat{j} + 8\hat{k}$.

Equating the $\hat{j}$ components:

$4 + 4\alpha = 12$

$4\alpha = 8$

$\alpha = 2$

Equating the $\hat{k}$ components also gives $6 + \alpha = 8 \implies \alpha = 2$.

Answer: $2$

questions.q: A block of mass $m = 4$ kg is placed on top of a block of mass $M = 2$ kg. The lower block $M$ rests on a frictionless horizontal surface. A horizontal spring of spring constant $k = 120$ N/m is attached to the UPPER block $m$ and a rigid wall. The coefficient of static friction between the two blocks is $\mu = 0.3$. If the system is set into oscillation, what is the maximum amplitude (in cm) for which the lower block does not slip relative to the upper block? (Take $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.question: A block of mass $m = 4$ kg is placed on top of a block of mass $M = 2$ kg. The lower block $M$ rests on a frictionless horizontal surface. A horizontal spring of spring constant $k = 120$ N/m is attached to the UPPER block $m$ and a rigid wall. The coefficient of static friction between the two blocks is $\mu = 0.3$. If the system is set into oscillation, what is the maximum amplitude (in cm) for which the lower block does not slip relative to the upper block? (Take $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
When the two blocks oscillate together without slipping, they move with a common acceleration. The angular frequency of the system is:
$\omega^2 = \dfrac{k}{M+m} = \dfrac{120}{2+4} = \dfrac{120}{6} = 20 \text{ rad/s}^2$

Since the spring is attached to the upper block, the only horizontal force acting on the lower block $M$ is the static friction between the two blocks. For the lower block to not slip, the required frictional force must be less than or equal to the limiting static friction.

The limiting static friction depends on the normal force between the blocks, which is determined by the mass of the upper block:
$f_{\max} = \mu m g = 0.3 \times 4 \times 10 = 12 \text{ N}$

The maximum acceleration that this friction can provide to the lower block is:
$a_{\max} = \dfrac{f_{\max}}{M} = \dfrac{12}{2} = 6 \text{ m/s}^2$

In SHM, the maximum acceleration is related to the amplitude $A$ by $a_{\max} = \omega^2 A$. Substituting the values:
$6 = 20 \times A$
$A = \dfrac{6}{20} = 0.3 \text{ m}$

Converting to centimeters:
$A = 0.3 \times 100 = 30 \text{ cm}$

Answer: $30$

questions.q: A uniform circular disc of radius $8\text{ cm}$ rotates about an axis perpendicular to its plane. If the radius of gyration of the disc about this axis is $9\text{ cm}$, the perpendicular distance of the axis from the centre of the disc is $x\text{ cm}$. The value of $x$ is _____.
questions.question: A uniform circular disc of radius $8\text{ cm}$ rotates about an axis perpendicular to its plane. If the radius of gyration of the disc about this axis is $9\text{ cm}$, the perpendicular distance of the axis from the centre of the disc is $x\text{ cm}$. The value of $x$ is _____.
questions.solution:
Let $M$ be the mass and $R$ be the radius of the disc.

The moment of inertia of the disc about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its plane is $I_{\text{cm}} = \dfrac{1}{2}MR^2$.

Let the axis of rotation be at a distance $d$ from the centre. By the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia about this axis is:

$I = I_{\text{cm}} + Md^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}MR^2 + Md^2$

We are given that the radius of gyration is $k$. Thus, $I = Mk^2$.

Equating the two expressions for $I$:

$Mk^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}MR^2 + Md^2$

$k^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}R^2 + d^2$

Substitute $R = 8\text{ cm}$ and $k = 9\text{ cm}$:

$9^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}(8)^2 + d^2$

$81 = 32 + d^2$

$d^2 = 49 \Rightarrow d = 7\text{ cm}$

Therefore, $x = 7$.

Answer: $7$
